IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r4.claim: Shuʿayb's people call him forbearing and prudent sarcastically, as one might call an idiot intelligent or a fool forbearing.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r4.anchor: قول قوم شعيب: إنك لأنت الحليم الرشيد [هود: 87]

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r5.claim: The poet's address 'O forbearing one' is sarcastic, accusing the person of failing to act gently.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r5.anchor: يا حلي ... م إنك لم تأس أسوا رفيقا

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The people mock Shu’ayb’s prayer as if it required abandoning ancestral worship and forbade using their wealth as they pleased; they sarcastically call him the only wise man.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Does your prayer teach you that we leave those which our forefathers used to worship or we should not use our wealth the way we want to?

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r1.claim: Shuʿayb's people mock his call to worship God alone and fair measure, asking whether his prayer orders them to abandon ancestral worship and control their wealth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r1.anchor: لما أمرهم شعيب بعبادة الله وترك عبادة أوثانهم، وبإيفاء المكيال والميزان، ردوا عليه على سبيل الاستهزاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r2.claim: They mocked his frequent prayer by winking and laughing whenever he prayed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r2.anchor: وكان كثير الصلاة، وكان إذا صلى تغامزوا وتضاحكوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r3.claim: Prayer's commanding is figurative: it either calls and urges toward good, as prayer is said to prohibit indecency, or they use the idea sarcastically to taunt him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r3.anchor: وكون الصلاة آمرة هو على وجه المجاز، كما كانت ناهية في قوله: إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r4.claim: The implied sense is that prayer commands you to impose on us that we abandon these practices; the omitted complement is needed because a person cannot order another's act directly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r4.anchor: والمعنى: فأمرك بتكليفنا أن نترك، فحذف المضاف لأن الإنسان لا يؤمر بفعل غيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r5.claim: The apparent meaning of صلاتك is the formal prayer prescribed in that prophetic law.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r5.anchor: والظاهر أنه أريد بالصلاة الصلاة المعهودة في تلك الشريعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says God never sent a prophet without prescribing prayer and almsgiving for him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن: لم يبعث الله نبيا إلا فرض عليه الصلاة والزكاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r7.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r7.claim: Other explanations identify صلاتك as your recitation, your mosques, or your supplications.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: أريد قراءتك. وقيل: مساجدك. وقيل: دعواتك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r8.speaker: ابن وثاب، والأخوان، وحفص
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r8.claim: Ibn Waththāb, the two Kūfan readers, and Ḥafṣ read أصلاتك in the singular.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب والأخوان وحفص: أصلاتك على التوحيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r9.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r9.claim: The majority read both verbs in أو أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء in the first-person plural.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: أو أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء بالنون فيهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r10.speaker: الضحاك بن قيس، وابن أبي عبلة، وزيد بن علي، وأبو عبد الرحمن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r10.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays, Ibn Abī ʿAbla, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, and a report from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read both verbs in the second person.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك بن قيس، وابن أبي عبلة، وزيد بن علي: بالتاء فيهما على الخطاب، ورويت عن أبي عبد الرحمن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r11.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن وطلحة وابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r11.claim: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Ṭalḥa read نفعل in the first person but ما تشاء in the second; this is also reported from Ibn ʿAbbās.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p196#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن وطلحة: نفعل بالنون، ما نشاء بالتاء على الخطاب، ورويت عن ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r1.claim: With the two nūn readings, the clause about what they do with their wealth coordinates with what their fathers worship, meaning they ask whether to abandon it and keep their practices.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r1.anchor: فمن قرأ بالنون فيهما فقوله: أو أن نفعل معطوف على قوله: ما يعبد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r2.claim: With tāʾ in both verbs, or nūn in both, the clause coordinates with ‘leave’: Shuʿayb commands them to leave ancestral worship and, by the readings, their own or his conduct with wealth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r2.anchor: ومن قرأ بالتاء فيهما أو بالنون فيهما فمعطوف على أن نترك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r3.claim: The disjunctive particle indicates variation, as Shuʿayb commands one thing at one time and another at another; another view gives it the sense of ‘and.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r3.anchor: وأو للتنويع أي: تأمرك مرة بهذا، ومرة بهذا. وقيل: بمعنى الواو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r4.claim: The apparent meaning of their conduct with wealth is the previously mentioned short measure and weight.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r4.anchor: والظاهر أن الذي كانوا يفعلونه في أموالهم هو بخس الكيل والوزن المقدم ذكره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r5.speaker: محمد بن كعب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says they clipped dinars and dirhams, then passed them off alongside sound coins as fraud.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r5.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب: قرضهم الدينار والدرهم، وإجراء ذلك مع الصحيح على جهة التدليس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r6.speaker: ابن المسيب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r6.claim: Ibn al-Musayyib regards cutting dinars and dirhams as corruption in the land.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r6.anchor: وعن ابن المسيب: قطع الدنانير والدراهم من الفساد في الأرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r7.claim: Another view identifies the misconduct as changing currency types in order to consume people's property unlawfully.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r7.anchor: وقيل: تبديل السكك التي يقصد بها أكل أموال الناس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r8.claim: With tāʾ in both verbs or in ‘we wish,’ the apparent reading is that Shuʿayb required full measure and weight; Sufyan al-Thawri instead says he ordered almsgiving.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r8.anchor: ومن قرأ بالتاء فيهما أو في نشاء، والظاهر أنه إيفاء المكيال والميزان. وقال سفيان الثوري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r9.claim: Their description of Shuʿayb as forbearing and right-minded may be sincere praise, challenging how such a person could oppose ancestral religion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r9.anchor: فيحتمل أن يريدوا بذلك الحقيقة أي: إنك للمتصف بهذين الوصفين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r10.claim: The words may mean ‘forbearing and right-minded by your own claim,’ since he commands them as he does.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r10.anchor: أو يحتمل أن يريدوا بذلك إنك لأنت الحليم الرشيد بزعمك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r11.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r11.claim: Qatada reads the compliment as mockery and sarcasm, implying that Shuʿayb is actually rash and foolish.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r11.anchor: أن قالوا ذلك على سبيل الاستهزاء والتهكم، قاله قتادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r12.claim: Their apparent praise indirectly imputes rashness and foolishness, like calling a miser generous or an Abyssinian ‘father of the white one.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r12.anchor: والمراد: نسبته إلى الطيش والعي كما تقول للشحيح: لو رآك حاتم لسجد لك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r13.claim: Shuʿayb's reply is a subtle, gentle appeal meant to win them over and draw them down from opposition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r13.anchor: يا قوم أرأيتم إن كنت هذه مراجعة لطيفة واستنزال حسن، واستدعاء رقيق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r14.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r14.claim: The Prophet called Shuʿayb ‘the orator of the prophets.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r14.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ذلك خطيب الأنبياء»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r15.claim: Rhetoricians call this technique drawing the addressee in; it is a subtle way to reach one's aim, also found in the stories of Abraham, Noah, Hud, Salih, and the believer from Pharaoh's people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p197/r15.anchor: وهذا النوع يسمى استدراج المخاطب عند أرباب علم البيان، وهو نوع لطيف غريب المغزى

THALABI:v5p186/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p186/r1.speaker: أهل التفسير
THALABI:v5p186/r1.claim: The exegetes say Shuayb had forbidden the people to manipulate money, and they were punished for cutting dinars and dirhams.
THALABI:v5p186/r1.anchor: قال أهل التفسير: كان هذا نهيا لهم عنه وعذبوا لأجله قطع الدنانير والدراهم

THALABI:v5p186/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p186/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p186/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the sarcastic description al-halim al-rashid as meaning foolish and misguided.

THALABI:v5p186/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p186/r3.speaker: القاضي
THALABI:v5p186/r3.claim: The judge explains that Arabs sometimes call something by its opposite as a favorable omen or euphemism, as when they call a bitten person safe or a mouse a place of escape.
THALABI:v5p186/r3.anchor: قال القاضي: والعرب تصف الشيء بضده، للتطير والفأل كما قيل للديغ: سليم، وللفأرة: مفازة

THALABI:v5p186/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p186/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p186/r4.claim: Another view takes the phrase as mockery, like ironic names or the firekeepers' address to Abu Jahl; the author cites the latter's scriptural wording.
THALABI:v5p186/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو على الاستهزاء، كقولهم للحبشي: أبو البيضاء، وللأبيض: أبو الجون

THALABI:v5p186/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p186/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p186/r5.claim: A further reported reading means “the forbearing and rightly guided, as you claim,” continuing the sarcasm directed at Shuayb.
THALABI:v5p186/r5.anchor: يم الرشيد بزعمك وعند كن ومثله في صفة أبي جهل

THALABI:v5p186/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p186/r6.speaker: ابن كيسان
THALABI:v5p186/r6.claim: Ibn Kaysan takes the description literally: Shuayb is forbearing and rightly guided, so it ill suits him to break his people's unity or oppose their religion.
THALABI:v5p186/r6.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: هو على الصحة أي أنك يا شعيب لنا حليم رشيد

STUDYQURAN:11:87/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:87/r1.speaker: Some commentators
STUDYQURAN:11:87/r1.claim: Some commentators take the Midianites’ question about Shuʿayb’s prayers as mockery.
STUDYQURAN:11:87/r1.anchor: Some commentators note that the Midianites’ question here is a form of mockery (Kl, Q).

STUDYQURAN:11:87/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:87/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:11:87/r2.claim: Q says the sarcastic praise suggests Shuʿayb has forbearance and sound judgment only in his own estimation.
STUDYQURAN:11:87/r2.anchor: they intimate that he has these qualities only in his own opinion (Q). The implication is thus that the Midianites

STUDYQURAN:11:87/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:87/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:11:87/r3.claim: The arrogant Midianites dismissed Shuʿayb’s message and called him bewitched and a liar.
STUDYQURAN:11:87/r3.anchor: The implication is thus that the Midianites, who were arrogant (7:88), did not take seriously Shuʿayb’s message, instead referring to him as

TAB-FULL:v12p545/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p545/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p545/r1.claim: The people ask whether Shuaib's prayer commands them to abandon the idols and images worshipped by their fathers.
TAB-FULL:v12p545/r1.anchor: عبادة {ما يعبد آباؤنا} [هود: 62] من الأوثان والأصنام،

TAB-FULL:v12p545/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p545/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p545/r2.claim: They object to being stopped from doing as they wished with their money, including clipping coins and shorting people in measure and weight.
TAB-FULL:v12p545/r2.anchor: من كسر الدراهم وقطعها، وبخس الناس في الكيل والوزن؛

TAB-FULL:v12p545/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p545/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p545/r3.claim: A forbearing person is not driven by anger to do what he would not do while calm.
TAB-FULL:v12p545/r3.anchor: وهو الذي لا يحمله الغضب أن يفعل ما لم يكن ليفعله في حال الرضا

TAB-FULL:v12p545/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p545/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p545/r4.claim: They call him soundly guided because he directs them to abandon idol worship.
TAB-FULL:v12p545/r4.anchor: يعني: رشيد الأمر في أمره إياهم أن يتركوا عبادة الأوثان

TAB-FULL:v12p545/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p545/r5.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TAB-FULL:v12p545/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reports that Shuaib prohibited clipping or cutting dirhams; the transmitter is unsure which wording he used.
TAB-FULL:v12p545/r5.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم، في قوله: " {أو أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء} [هود: 87] قال: كان مما نهاهم عنه: حذف الدراهم

TAB-FULL:v12p545/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p545/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
TAB-FULL:v12p545/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi says Shuaib's people were punished for cutting dirhams, citing their objection in this verse.
TAB-FULL:v12p545/r6.anchor: سمعت محمد بن كعب القرظي، يقول: " بلغني أن قوم شعيب عذبوا في قطع الدراهم

TAB-FULL:v12p545/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p545/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v12p545/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says Shuaib prohibited cutting dinars and dirhams, while the people claimed they could cut, burn, or discard their own money as they wished.
TAB-FULL:v12p545/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {قالوا يا شعيب أصلاتك تأمرك

TAB-FULL:v12p546/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p546/r1.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TAB-FULL:v12p546/r1.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reports that clipping dirhams was among the things Shuaib forbade.
TAB-FULL:v12p546/r1.anchor: قال زيد: كان من ذلك قطع الدراهم

TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r1.speaker: الأعمش
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r1.claim: Al-Aʿmash glosses Shuaib's prayer as his recitation.
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r1.anchor:
عن الأعمش، في قوله
: " {أصلاتك} [هود: 87] قال: قراءتك

TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r2.speaker: بعض البصريين
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r2.claim: The Basran reading supplies a second أن نترك: does your prayer command us to abandon our fathers' worship or to abandon doing as we please with our wealth?
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r2.anchor: فقال بعض البصريين: معنى ذلك: أصلاتك تأمرك أن نترك ما يعبد آباؤنا، أو أن نترك أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء

TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r3.speaker: بعض الكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r3.claim: Some Kufans agree with that parse and offer another: the question contrasts prayer commanding one thing with forbidding another, and attaches the second phrase to ما يعبد.
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعض الكوفيين نحو هذا القول، قال: وفيها وجه آخر يجعل الأمر كالنهي،

TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r4.speaker: بعض الكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r4.claim: In the alternative Kufan parse, the first أن is governed by تأمرك and the second is coordinated with ما in ما يعبد.
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r4.anchor: فهي حينئذ مردودة على أن الأولى منصوبة بقوله «تأمرك» ، وأن الثانية منصوبة عطفا بها على «ما» التي في قوله: {ما يعبد}

TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r5.speaker: بعض القراء
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r5.claim: Some readers are reported to read ما تشاء, making the second أن clause coordinate directly with the first.
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r5.anchor: وقد ذكر عن بعض القراء أنه قرأه «ما تشاء» ، فمن قرأ ذلك كذلك، فلا مؤنة فيه

TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r6.claim: Al-Tabari says the hostile people used الحليم الرشيد sarcastically to mock, belittle, and portray Shuaib as foolish.
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r6.anchor: فإنهم أعداء الله قالوا ذلك له استهزاء به؛

TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj says their description of Shuaib as forbearing and rightly guided was mockery.
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن جريج " {إنك لأنت الحليم الرشيد} [هود: 87] قال: يستهزئون "

TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd likewise says they mocked him by calling him forbearing and rightly guided.
TAB-FULL:v12p546#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {إنك لأنت الحليم الرشيد} [هود: 87] المستهزئون يستهزئون بأنك لأنت الحليم الرشيد "

TABATABAI:11:86-88/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:86-88/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:86-88/r4.claim: They claim freedom to choose their religion and dispose of their own wealth, denying that Shuʿayb has authority to command or forbid them.
TABATABAI:11:86-88/r4.anchor: أنا في حرية فيما نختاره لأنفسنا من دين أو نتصرف به في أموالنا من وجوه التصرف

TABATABAI:11:86-88/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:86-88/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:86-88/r5.claim: They cast their objection as a finely shaped, mocking and reproachful rhetorical question.
TABATABAI:11:86-88/r5.anchor: وقد أدوا مرادهم هذا في صورة بديعة مشوبة بالتهكم واللوم معا ومسبوكة في قالب الاستفهام الإنكاري

TABATABAI:11:86-88/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:86-88/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:86-88/r6.claim: They attribute the command to prayer because it urges Shuʿayb to oppose their idol worship and short measure; he answers by describing his instruction as a prohibition.
TABATABAI:11:86-88/r6.anchor: لما فيها من البعث والدعوة إلى معارضة القوم في عبادتهم الأصنام ونقصهم المكيال والميزان

TABATABAI:11:87-88/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:87-88/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:87-88/r1.claim: Their demand that they abandon what their fathers worship implies an appeal to inherited national custom and the continuity of ancestral religion.
TABATABAI:11:87-88/r1.anchor: ليشيروا بذلك إلى الحجة في ذلك وهي أن هذه الأصنام دام على عبادتها آباؤنا فهي سنة قومية لنا

TABATABAI:11:87-88/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:87-88/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:87-88/r2.claim: Calling the wealth their own implies that an owner may manage it as he wishes and that others may not interfere; skill and ingenuity guide livelihood.
TABATABAI:11:87-88/r2.anchor: فذكروا الأموال مضافة إلى أنفسهم ليكون في ذلك إيماء إلى الحجة

TABATABAI:11:87-88/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:87-88/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:87-88/r3.claim: The mockery lies in making prayer command Shuʿayb to make them abandon their practice and in assigning the command to prayer itself.
TABATABAI:11:87-88/r3.anchor: إلا أن التهكم في تعليقهم أمر الصلاة شعيبا على تركهم ما يعبد آباؤهم، وكذا في نسبه الأمر إلى الصلاة لا غير

TABATABAI:11:87-88/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:87-88/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:87-88/r4.claim: Their praise of his forbearance and sound judgment is sincere; the emphatic particles and nominal clause sharpen their rebuke that such a person should demand a foolish infringement on freedom.
TABATABAI:11:87-88/r4.anchor: ولذلك أكد قوله { إنك لأنت الحليم الرشيد } بإن واللام وإتيان الخبر جملة اسمية

TABATABAI:11:87-88/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:87-88/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:87-88/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects the common interpretation that they sarcastically called Shuʿayb forbearing and right-minded while meaning the opposite, ignorance and error.
TABATABAI:11:87-88/r5.anchor: أنه موصوف بضدهما وهو الجهالة والغي. ليس بصواب.

TABRISI:11:87/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:87/r1.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير أبي بكر
TABRISI:11:87/r1.claim: The Kufans except Abū Bakr read the word in the singular, without wāw.
TABRISI:11:87/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير أبي بكر أصلاتك بغير واو على التوحيد

TABRISI:11:87/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:87/r2.speaker: الباقون
TABRISI:11:87/r2.claim: The remaining readers use the plural form with wāw.

TABRISI:11:87/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:87/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:87/r17.claim: An-nasb in أو أن نفعل means ‘or [does it command] that we do’; it coordinates with ما يعبد آباؤنا, not أن نترك, which would make the sense defective.
TABRISI:11:87/r17.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون قوله { أن نفعل } معطوفا على قوله { أن نترك } لأن المعنى يصير فاسدا

TABRISI:11:87/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:87/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:87/r18.claim: Here أو has the alternative force of ‘sit with al-Ḥasan or Ibn Sīrīn’ and the cited statement that God is nearer to either rich or poor.
TABRISI:11:87/r18.anchor: وأو هنا بمنزلتها في قولك جالس الحسن أو ابن سيرين

TABRISI:11:84-95/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:84-95/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:11:84-95/r5.claim: The people mocked Shuʿayb's appeal because he prayed often and taught that prayer restrains evil and forbids indecency and wrongdoing.
TABRISI:11:84-95/r5.anchor: لأن شعيبا ع كان كثير الصلاة وكان يقول إذا صلى إن الصلاة رادعة عن الشر

TABRISI:11:84-95/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:84-95/r6.speaker: الحسن وعطاء وأبو مسلم
TABRISI:11:84-95/r6.claim: They meant ‘does your religion command you’; prayer stands for religion because it is among its most important practices.
TABRISI:11:84-95/r6.anchor: معناه أدينك يأمرك بترك دين السلف عن الحسن وعطاء وأبي مسلم

TABRISI:11:84-95/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:84-95/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:84-95/r7.claim: They spoke about Shuʿayb's prayer in mockery.
TABRISI:11:84-95/r7.anchor: وإنما قالوا ذلك على وجه الاستهزاء

TABRISI:11:84-95/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:84-95/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:84-95/r8.claim: They ask whether his prayer commands them to leave their fathers' worship or to stop doing what they wish with their wealth, including cheating and short measure.
TABRISI:11:84-95/r8.anchor: أصلاتك تأمرك بترك عبادة ما يعبد آباؤنا أو بترك فعل ما نشاء

TABRISI:11:84-95/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:84-95/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:11:84-95/r9.claim: On one view the praise is sarcastic and means the opposite: foolish and astray.
TABRISI:11:84-95/r9.anchor: قيل: إنهم قالوا ذلك على وجه الهزؤ والتهكم وأرادوا به ضد ذلك

TABRISI:11:84-95/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:84-95/r10.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:11:84-95/r10.claim: Alternatively they meant the praise sincerely: as a patient leader among his people, he should not oppose them.
TABRISI:11:84-95/r10.anchor: وقيل: إنهم قالوا ذلك على التحقيق أي أنك أنت الحليم في قومك

TABRISI:11:84-95/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:84-95/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:84-95/r11.claim: Ḥalīm is one who does not hasten to punish someone who deserves it; rashīd is one who guides.
TABRISI:11:84-95/r11.anchor: والحليم الذي لا يعاجل بالعقوبة مستحقها والرشيد المرشد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r1.claim: The word is also read in the singular; the discussion of both readings was given under 9:103.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r1.anchor: وتقرأ (أصلاتك) على واحدة، وتوجيه القراءتين (¬2) ذكرناه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r2.claim: They mean: does your religion command you? Prayer stands for religion because they saw it as a religious practice.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r2.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس (¬4): يريدون دينك يأمرك، وعلى # هذا كنى عن الدين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r3.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r3.claim: Al-Hasan gives the same interpretation: they ask whether his religion commands him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r3.anchor: وهو معنى قول الحسن (¬1)، وروي عن ابن عباس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r4.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas says Shuayb prayed often, which is why they spoke of his prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r4.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس (¬2) أيضا أنه قال: كان شعيب كثير الصلاة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r5.claim: Their statement shows they worshiped gods other than God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬4): وهذا دليل (¬5) على أنهم كانوا يعبدون غير الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r6.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r6.claim: Prayer does not literally command; it causes the action associated with it, as in 29:45, because prayer is part of faith and faith restrains wrongdoing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r6.anchor: قال صاحب النظم: قوله: {أصلاتك تأمرك} وليس للصلاة أمر ولا نهي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r7.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r7.claim: The command is really Shuayb's command to them; the wording omits a repeated command, meaning does your prayer make you command us to leave these practices?
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p523/r7.anchor: فأما قوله: {تأمرك أن نترك} أوقع الأمر على شعيب وهو في المعنى واقع على قومه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r1.claim: The ancestors are dead, but their past worship is expressed in the present tense and means what they used to worship, as in 2:102.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r1.anchor: وقد خلوا وماتوا وجاءت الحكاية عن فعلهم على وزن الاستقبال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbari, along with al-Farra and al-Zajjaj, coordinates أن with ما: or that we do.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r2.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري (¬1): (أن) منسوقة على (ما) في قوله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r3.claim: Al-Farra also proposes an omitted verb: does your prayer command us to leave our ancestors' worship and forbid us to do this? The command implies the omitted prohibition, like cold implied by heat in 16:81.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r3.anchor: وزاد الفراء قولا آخر شرحه أبو بكر، وهو: أن تكون (أن) منصوبة بفعل مضمر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r4.claim: Doing what they wished with their money meant cheating, injustice, and short measure or weight.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r4.anchor: قال الكلبي (¬5): أي من البخس والظلم ونقص المكيال والميزان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers the explanation that they had mutually agreed to cheat one another.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r5.anchor: وهو اختيار الزجاج (¬6)؛ قال: المعنى: إنا قد تراضينا بالبخس فيما بيننا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r6.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطاء، القرظي، زيد بن أسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r6.claim: These authorities say Shuayb forbade them from cutting or debasing dinars and dirhams.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p525/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس (¬7) في رواية عطاء: يريد قطع الدنانير والدراهم، وهو # قول القرظي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas takes their praise as irony: they mean that Shuayb is foolish and ignorant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬3). يريدون: السفيه الجاهل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r2.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r2.claim: Abu Bakr says the ironic interpretation fits Arabic usage: calling someone sensible can mean he is a fool or ignorant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r2.anchor: قال أبو بكر: وهذا التفسير مشاكل للغة (¬4)؛ لأن العربي يقول لمخاطبه إذا استحمقه: يا عاقل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r3.speaker: الشاعر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r3.claim: An anonymous poet's ironic address يا حليم is clarified by the line's ending, which shows the addressee was being called ignorant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r3.anchor: قال الشاعر (¬6): فقلت لسيدنا يا حليم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r4.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r4.claim: Muqatil explains the ironic words as foolish and astray.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r4.anchor: هذا قول مقاتل بن سليمان (¬8) قال: معناه: إنك لأنت السفيه الضال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r5.speaker: الحسن، ابن جريج، الكلبي، ابن زيد وأكثر أهل التأويل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r5.claim: Al-Hasan, Ibn Jurayj, al-Kalbi, Ibn Zayd, and most exegetes take the statement as mockery of Shuayb.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن وابن جريج (¬9) والكلبي وابن زيد وأكثر أهل التأويل: هذا # على طريق الاستهزاء بشعيب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r6.speaker: ابن كيسان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r6.claim: Ibn Kaysan takes the words as sincere praise: they call Shuayb forbearing and right-guided, and imply that it does not suit him to divide his people and oppose their religion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p526/r6.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان (¬1): هذا على طريق الصحة، قالوا له: إنك فينا حليم رشيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p416/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p416/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p416/r1.claim: The Companions witnessed revelation and knew its interpretation as native speakers of Arabic.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p416/r1.anchor: فالصحابة الذين نزل فيهم القرآن شاهدوا التنزيل، وعرفوا التأويل؛ لأنهم أهل اللغة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p416/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p416/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p416/r2.claim: The Successors and early pious authorities did not contrive their collections or strain to chase remote hidden meanings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p416/r2.anchor: وأما التابعون والسلف الصالحون فإنهم لم يتصنعوا في جمع ما جمعوا، ولم يتكلفوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p416/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p416/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p416/r3.claim: Scholars of meanings focused on grammatical parsing and explaining modes of discourse; later writers differ in rank and purpose, and few closely align wording with exegesis in a consistent, fluent way.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p416/r3.anchor: وأرباب المعاني (¬2) اقتصروا على الإعراب، وبيان نهج الخطاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p416/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p416/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p416/r4.claim: Although earlier scholars left little unexplored, later authors can gather scattered pearls with subtle skill, arranging them attractively and earning praise and reward.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p416/r4.anchor: غير أن المتأخر بلطيف حيلته (¬1)، ودقيق (¬2) فطنته، يلتقط الدرر ويجمع الغرر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p416/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p416/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p416/r5.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says he worked to establish the discipline's foundations and learned language from Aḥmad b. Muḥammad al-ʿArūḍī, a veteran lexicographer who studied and transmitted from major language authorities including al-Azharī.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p416/r5.anchor: أما (اللغة): فقد درستها على الشيخ أبي الفضل أحمد بن محمد بن عبدالله بن يوسف العروضي

QASHANI:11:88/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:88/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:88/r2.claim: Shuayb turns to his argument after their defiant rejection and mockery of his worship, monotheism, and renunciation, including their taunt about his prayer.
QASHANI:11:88/r2.anchor: ولما شاهد إنكارهم وعتوهم في العصيان، واستهزاءهم بطاعته، وزهده وتوحيده وتنزهه بقولهم: { أصلاتك } إلى آخره

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:84-87/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:84-87/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:84-87/r8.claim: They mean Shuayb's religion when they speak of his prayers commanding him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:84-87/r8.anchor: يريدون: دينك يأمرك، أي: أفي دينك الأمر بذا؟

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:84-87/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:84-87/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:84-87/r9.claim: They object to being forbidden from cheating, wrongdoing, and reducing measures and weights.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:84-87/r9.anchor: من البخس والظلم، ونقص المكيال والميزان

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:84-87/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:84-87/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:84-87/r10.claim: They call him foolish and ignorant, using 'forbearing and rightly guided' sarcastically.

ELMALILI:11:87/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:87/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:87/r1.claim: Shuaib prayed frequently and was known for this practice.

ELMALILI:11:87/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:87/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:87/r2.claim: Prayer, the pillar of religion, is burdensome except for the humble, as the verse in al-Baqara states.
ELMALILI:11:87/r2.anchor: medlûlünce hâşi‘înden mâ‘adâsının pek ağırına gelen

ELMALILI:11:87/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:87/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:87/r3.claim: Those unable to grasp the joy and sublimity of standing and prostrating before God regard prayer as a futile, useless burden.
ELMALILI:11:87/r3.anchor: Allah’ın huzûrunda divan durmanın, secdelere kapanmanın zevk ve ulviyetini idrak edemeyenlere beyhûde, fâidesiz bir külfetten ibaret görünen büyük bir amel

ELMALILI:11:87/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:87/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:87/r4.claim: Mocking those who pray is characteristic of disbelief and of rebellious unbelievers.
ELMALILI:11:87/r4.anchor: namaz kılanlarla eğlenmek küfrün muktezâsı ve azgın kâfirlerin mu‘tâdıdır

ELMALILI:11:87/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:87/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:87/r5.claim: By attributing his teaching to prayer, they reject Shuaib's monotheistic, legal, and ethical message, attack his reason and discernment, and mock his prophethood.
ELMALILI:11:87/r5.anchor: bunları bilhassa onun namazına isnad ederek akl ü rüşdüne taarruz ve nübüvvetiyle istihzâ ediyorlar

ELMALILI:11:87/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:87/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:87/r6.claim: They regard worshipping only God and respecting justice in trade and politics as foolish restrictions on freedom.
ELMALILI:11:87/r6.anchor: Yalnız Allah’a ibadet edip türlü türlü mâbudlara kul olmaktan kurtulmayı

ELMALILI:11:87/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:87/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:87/r7.claim: Shuaib did not prohibit people from disposing of their own wealth as they wished; he prohibited wronging other people's property, thereby affirming rather than curtailing freedom.
ELMALILI:11:87/r7.anchor: Şuayb aleyhisselâm onlara “mallarınızda istediğiniz gibi tasarruf etmeyin” dememişti, “nâsın eşyâsına haksızlık yapmayın” demişti. Bu ise hürriyeti men‘değil, tesbit ve teyit oluyordu

ELMALILI:11:87/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:87/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:87/r8.claim: Unless everyone's property and rights are protected, no one can feel secure in their rights or freely manage their own wealth.
ELMALILI:11:87/r8.anchor: herkesin emvâli ve hukūku mahfuz olmadıkça kimse hakkından emin olamaz, emvâlinde dilediği gibi tasarruf yapamaz

ELMALILI:11:87/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:87/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:87/r9.claim: The people treat others' wealth as their own and seek to exploit whatever their power permits, presenting the demand for justice as a constraint on their liberty.
ELMALILI:11:87/r9.anchor: onlar nâsın mallarını kendi malları imiş gibi farz ediyorlar, güçlerinin yetebildiği tecavüzü yapmak istiyorlar

ELMALILI:11:87/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:87/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:87/r10.claim: Their question is sophistry and taunting: they sarcastically call him sensible while pretending that prayer tells them to abandon ancestral worship and unrestricted exploitation.
ELMALILI:11:87/r10.anchor: “emvâlimizde dilediğimizi yapmaktan vazgeçmemizi namazın mı emrediyor, sofu sen ne akıllısın be!” gibi mugālata ile târiz ve istihzâya kalkışıyorlar

ELMALILI:11:87/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:87/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:87/r11.claim: Idolatry, arrogant contempt for prayer, and sophistry that invokes liberty and trade to excuse fraud, aggression, insolence, and corruption recur among modern unbelievers; contemporary people should heed Shuaib and Midian.
ELMALILI:11:87/r11.anchor: medeniyet-i hâzıra insanları kıssa-i Şuayb ve Medyen’i pek ziyade nazar-ı ibret ile dinlemelidirler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r1.claim: The commentary translates salat as worship.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r2.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r2.claim: Shawkani also interprets salat as religion or recitation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r2.anchor: salât kelimesi “din, okuma” gibi anlamlarda da yorumlanmıştır (Şevkânî, II, 589)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r3.claim: Because worship expresses the monotheistic religion and opposition to idolatry, pagans mock believers' worship to undermine or weaken their religion; Shuaib's people did likewise.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r3.anchor: putperestler daima müminlerin ibadetiyle alay ederek dini yıkmaya, yıkamadıkları takdirde ise zayıflatmaya çalışmışlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r4.claim: Shuaib's worship and trade ethics suited human nature and promoted freedom, but his people ridiculed them as foolish restrictions.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r4.anchor: insan fıtratına uygun ve hürriyeti geliştirici davranışlar olduğu halde, onlar bunun hürriyeti engelleyici bir budalalık olduğunu düşünerek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r5.claim: Freedom is impossible without the security of life and property; Shuaib's divine rules aimed to provide that security.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r5.anchor: mal ve can güvenliğinin bulunmadığı yerde hürriyetten söz etmek mümkün değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r6.claim: Those accustomed to exploiting society through fraud wanted freedom only for themselves, including freedom to keep cheating, and thought the prophet would permit it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r6.anchor: hürriyeti sadece kendileri için istiyor ve istedikleri gibi yolsuzluk yapma hürriyetini savunuyorlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r7.claim: Their words imply that they thought a sensible person should not challenge established customs, which is why they found Shuaib's warnings strange.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r7.anchor: aklı başında bir kimsenin –yanlış da olsa– toplum içinde yerleşmiş gelenek ve göreneklere karşı çıkmasının doğru olmadığına inandıkları

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r8.claim: The phrase may instead have been mockery; their earlier ridicule suggests they did not really consider Shuaib sensible.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:87/r8.anchor: Bununla birlikte bu sözü Şuayb ile alay etmek için söylemiş olmaları ihtimali de vardır

QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r1.claim: People who fail to understand treat their acts as small, but the gravity of an act comes from opposing the Almighty, not from its size; a little lawful provision is better than much that ends in ruin.
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r1.anchor: وليس قدر الأجرام لأعيانها ، ولكن لمخالفة الجبار عظم شأنها ، قال تعالى : { وتحسبونه هينا وهو عند الله عظيم }

BURHAN:v1p140/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p140/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p140/r6.claim: أو أن, with hamza before waw, occurs in Hud, Bani Israil, Ta Ha, and al-Mumin; examples include Hud and al-Mumin.

BURHAN:v2p342/r13.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p342/r13.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p342/r13.claim: The fourteenth use is mockery or sarcasm, as in Shuʿayb's people's taunt and the challenge to the idols to speak.
BURHAN:v2p342/r13.anchor: الرابع عشر التهكم والاستهزاء ﴿ أصلاتك تأمرك ﴾ 5 ﴿ ألا تأكلون ما لكم لا تنطقون ﴾ 6

BURHAN:v1p79/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p79/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p79/r2.claim: The taunt's ending fits its opening: worship and control of wealth prepare the ideas of forbearance and sound judgment, especially in managing money.
BURHAN:v1p79/r2.anchor: لما تقدم ذكر العبادة والتصرف فى الأموال كان ذلك تمهيدا تاما لذكر الحلم والرشد

BURHAN:v4p54/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p54/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p54/r2.claim: Speech may address someone according to the addressee's belief rather than reality; the people ironically call Shuʿayb forbearing and rightly guided.
BURHAN:v4p54/r2.anchor: وقوله ﴿ لأنت الحليم الرشيد ﴾ 4 أي بزعمك واعتقادي

ITQAN:v4p449/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p449/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p449/r1.claim: In the orthographic list of hamzas written on waw, the phrase from Shuaib’s people includes ما نشاء.
ITQAN:v4p449/r1.anchor: ( في أموالنا ما نشؤا ) و ( ما دعؤا ) في غافر

ITQAN:v2p412/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p412/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p412/r6.claim: Al-ṣalah can mean religion or religious practice.

ITQAN:v2p529/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p529/r1.speaker: ابن هشام
ITQAN:v2p529/r1.claim: Ibn Hisham rejects coordinating أن نفعل with أن نترك: the speakers are not told to do as they wish; it coordinates with ما, so the sense is leaving both ancestral worship and their chosen financial conduct.
ITQAN:v2p529/r1.anchor: قال ابن هشام وقد زلت أقدام كثير من المعربين راعوا في الإعراب ظاهر اللفظ ولم ينظروا في موجب المعنى

ITQAN:v3p215/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p215/r15.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p215/r15.claim: Interrogation can be sarcastic or mocking: the people of Shuʿayb deride his prayer, and Abraham asks why the idols neither eat nor speak.
ITQAN:v3p215/r15.anchor: الثلاثون التهكم والاستهزاء نحو ﴿ أصلاتك تأمرك ﴾

ITQAN:v3p270#4/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p270#4/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p270#4/r1.claim: Tamkīn prepares a sentence ending so it fits securely and completes the meaning; removing it disrupts understanding. Here ‘forbearing’ suits worship and ‘right-minded’ suits financial conduct.
ITQAN:v3p270#4/r1.anchor: فالتمكين ويسمى ائتلاف القافية أن يمهد الناثر للقرينة أو الشاعر للقافية

ITQAN:v3p124/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p124/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p124/r4.claim: An oppositional metaphor joins meanings that cannot coexist; its taunting subtypes use a word for its opposite, as in ‘glad tidings’ for warning, ironic praise of Shuʿayb’s opponents, and ‘the mighty, noble’ for humiliation.
ITQAN:v3p124/r4.anchor: ومن العنادية التهكمية والتمليحية وهما ما استعمل في ضد أو نقيض

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r1.claim: The first poem says not to expect the addressees to see the speaker’s honoring them coexist with their humiliating him.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r1.anchor: المعنى : لا تطمعوا أن تروا إكرامنا ، وقد وجد مع إهانتكم وجامعها في الحصول

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r2.claim: Abū Tammām’s couplet is offered as a subtle instance of the same chapter on separation and connection.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r2.anchor: ومما له مأخذ لطيف في هذا الباب قول أبي تمام

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r3.claim: A clause that confirms or explains the previous clause can connect by meaning alone and needs no conjunction, just as an adjective or emphatic phrase connects directly to its noun.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r3.anchor: وتستغني بربط معناها لها عن حرف عطف يربطها

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r4.claim: In 2:2, لا ريب فيه confirms and reinforces ذلك الكتاب, effectively repeating the assertion, so it needs no conjunction.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r4.anchor: قوله ( ﴿ لا ريب فيه ﴾ ) بيان وتوكيد وتحقيق لقوله : ( ﴿ ذلك الكتاب ﴾ )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r5.claim: In 2:6, لا يؤمنون confirms that warning and non-warning are alike to the disbelievers; ختم الله على قلوبهم then confirms this more forcefully, since such a response implies a sealed heart.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r5.anchor: قوله تعالى : ( ﴿ لا يؤمنون ﴾ ) تأكيد لقوله : ( ﴿ سواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم ﴾ )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r6.claim: In 2:9, يخادعون الله has no conjunction because their claim to believe while lacking belief is itself the deception, not a separate action.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r6.anchor: إنما قال ( ﴿ يخادعون ﴾ ) ولم يقل : ويخادعون

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r7.claim: In 2:14, إنما نحن مستهزؤون restates إنا معكم: both mean they have not believed the Prophet or left Judaism, so the statements amount to the same thing.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p177/r7.anchor: وقولهم : ( ﴿ إنما نحن مستهزؤون ﴾ ) خبر بهذا المعنى بعينه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r1.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r1.claim: Abū Bakr recited the anonymous victory poem when Khalid’s letter reported the Persians’ defeat.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r1.anchor: وتمثل به أبو بكر الصديق رضوان الله عليه حين أتاه كتاب خالد بالفتح في هزيمة الأعاجم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r2.claim: The author singles out the placement of فاء in فقد لاقيتنا فرأيت حربا as a feature to inspect in the anonymous battle poem.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r2.anchor: انظر إلى موضع الفاء في قوله : ( فقد لاقيتنا فرأيت حربا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r3.claim: In al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Aḥnaf’s verse, the author draws attention to the placement of ثم and the following فاء in فقد جئنا خراسانا.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r4.claim: Ibn al-Dumaynah’s question تريدين قتلي؟ and answer قد ظفرت بذلك exemplify separation and resumption.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r4.anchor: انظر إلى الفصل والاستئناف في قوله : ( تريدين قتلي ؟ قد ظفرت بذلك )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r5.speaker: أبو حفص الشطرنجي
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r5.claim: Abū Ḥafṣ al-Shatranjī wrote the poem in the voice of ʿUlayya, Hārūn al-Rashīd’s sister, after al-Rashīd reproached her.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r5.anchor: ومثل قول أبي حفص الشطرنجي ، وقاله على لسان علية أخت الرشيد

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r6.claim: The position of قد كنت أحسب in Abū Ḥafṣ’s poem is an example of the placement of a resumption.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r6.anchor: انظر إلى قوله : ' قد كنت أحسب ' ، وإلى مكان هذا الاستئناف

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r7.claim: In Abū Duwād’s horse poem, the author points to the indefinite رماحا as a meaningful choice of wording.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r7.anchor: انظر إلى التنكير في قوله : ' كأن رماحا '

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r8.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r8.claim: Ibn al-Bawwāb’s four lines are added as another poetic specimen in this discussion of arrangement; this excerpt does not single out a particular feature in them.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p83/r8.anchor: ومثل قول ابن البواب ، + من مجزوء الوافر + : ( أتيتك عائذا بك منك لما ضاقت الحيل )

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r12.claim: Shuʿayb’s people use ṣalāt to mean his religion.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r12.anchor: والسادس : الدين . ومنه قوله تعالى في هود :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p351/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p351/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p351/r1.claim: Sulūk originally means entering, and it is extended metaphorically where context indicates another sense.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p351/r1.anchor: السلوك : الدخول ويستعار في مواضع تدل عليها القرينة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p346/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p346/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p346/r1.claim: Sayyid originally means one elevated by leadership and rank.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p346/r1.anchor: السيد في الأصل العالي بطريق الرئاسة والرفعة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p346/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p346/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p346/r3.claim: The second sense is a forbearing or gentle master; the source groups with it the phrase about John in 3:39.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p346/r3.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أنه في القرآن على وجهين

FARRA:v2p26/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p26/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p26/r1.claim: The people address Shuʿayb with الحليم الرشيد sarcastically.
FARRA:v2p26/r1.anchor: وقوله: (إنك لأنت الحليم الرشيد) استهزاء منهم به.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p255/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p255/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p255/r6.claim: The people of Shuʿayb use الصلاة to mean religion when they mockingly ask whether it commands him to abandon ancestral worship.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p255/r6.anchor: أصلاتك تأمرك أن نترك ما يعبد آباؤنا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p255/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p255/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p255/r7.claim: الصلاة is also said to mean recitation in the question about Shuʿayb.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p255/r7.anchor: والصلاة: الدين. قال تعالى حكاية عن قوم شعيب: أصلاتك

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r1.claim: An anonymous poem jussives وأستدرج by carrying over the syntactic position of أصالحكم, understood without the preceding لعلي.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r1.anchor: فجزم وأستدرج، وحمله على موضع أصالحكم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba says disputed forms either follow accepted grammar or reflect scribal spelling; in the first case Quran has no grammatical error, and in the second the scribe's fault is not the Messenger's.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r3.anchor: فإن كانت على مذاهب النحويين فليس هاهنا لحن

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r4.speaker: عائشة
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r4.claim: Aisha is cited for the view that some disputed forms are mistakes made by the copyist.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r4.anchor: كما ذكرت عائشة رضي الله عنها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r10.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r10.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r10.claim: The codex writes ما نشؤا with wāw after alif in Shuʿayb's verse, while the same form elsewhere lacks wāw, without a difference in meaning.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r10.anchor: بواو بعد الألف، وفي موضع آخر

NAHHAS:v2p298/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p298/r4.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v2p298/r4.claim: Al-Kisa'i parses the first أن as genitive after an understood باء.
NAHHAS:v2p298/r4.anchor: قال الكسائي موضعها خفض على إضمار الباء

NAHHAS:v2p298/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p298/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p298/r5.claim: The second أن is accusative and coordinated with ما: do you command us to leave ancestral worship, or not do what we wish with our property?
NAHHAS:v2p298/r5.anchor: ( أو أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء ) ( أن ) في موضع نصب لا غير عطف على ( ما )

NAHHAS:v2p298/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p298/r6.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v2p298/r6.claim: Al-Farra instead understands the sense as “or do you forbid us to do what we wish with our property?”
NAHHAS:v2p298/r6.anchor: وزعم الفراء أن التقدير أو تنهانا أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء

NAHHAS:v2p298/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p298/r7.speaker: الضحاك بن قيس
NAHHAS:v2p298/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak ibn Qays reads أن تفعل with second-person verbs; on this reading, the clause coordinates with the first أن.
NAHHAS:v2p298/r7.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك بن قيس ( أو أن تفعل في أموالنا ما تشاء ) بالتاء فان على هذه القراءة معطوفة على أن الأولى

NAHHAS:v2p298/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p298/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p298/r8.claim: The townspeople sarcastically call Shuayb forbearing and rightly guided; their question exposes ignorance or obstinacy, a reading supported by what precedes and follows.
NAHHAS:v2p298/r8.anchor: قال أبو جعفر قد ذكرناه وفيه زيادة هي أحسن مما تقدم ولأن ما قبلها يدل على صحتها

SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r1.claim: The earlier discussion of singular versus plural صلاة applies here as in 9:103.
SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r1.anchor: وتقدم الخلاف في قوله " أصلاتك " بالنسبة إلى الإفراد والجمع في سورة براءة

SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r2.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r2.claim: The common reading has first-person plural نـ in نفعل and نشاء; Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Ibn Abī ʿAbla, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays read both with second-person تـ.
SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r2.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي وابن أبي عبلة والضحاك بن قيس بتاء الخطاب فيهما

SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r3.claim: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Ṭalḥa read the first verb with nūn and the second with tāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن وطلحة الأول بالنون والثاني بالتاء

SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r4.claim: With nūn in both verbs, أن نفعل coordinates with the object of نترك, meaning they would leave doing what they wanted, including the previously mentioned fraud; أو means either variation or and, but it cannot coordinate with تأمرك's object without changing the sense.
SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r4.anchor: فمن قرأ بالنون فيهما عطفه على مفعول " نترك " وهو " ما " الموصولة/، والتقدير:

SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r5.claim: With tāʾ in both verbs, the clause can coordinate either with the object of تأمرك or نترك; the reading with nūn in نفعل but tāʾ in تشاء must coordinate with تأمرك.
SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r5.anchor: ومن قرأ بالتاء فيهما جاز أن يكون معطوفا على مفعول " تأمرك " ، وأن يكون معطوفا على مفعول " نترك "

SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r6.claim: The apparent sense of the tāʾ reading, especially tāʾ in تشاء, is that Shuʿayb commands them to give full measure and weight.
SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r6.anchor: والظاهر من حيث المعنى في قراءة التاء فيهما أو في " تشاء " أن المراد بقولهم ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī understands تأمرك أن نترك as commanding them to leave something, with an omitted noun, since one person cannot be ordered to perform another's action.
SAMIN-DURR:11:87/r7.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " المعنى: تأمرك بتكليف أن نترك، فحذف المضاف لأن الإنسان لا يؤمر بفعل غيره "

ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r7.claim: A variant reading is aṣalawātuka, with a long ā in ṣalawāt.

ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r8.claim: Their response shows that they worshipped gods other than God.
ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r8.anchor: هذا دليل أنهم كانوا يعبدون غير الله

ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r9.claim: Their complaint means that they had agreed among themselves to shortchange in their business dealings.
ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r9.anchor: المعنى إنا قد تراضينا بالبخس فيما بيننا

ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r10.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r10.claim: A reported explanation says Shuʿayb forbade them to clip or break coins.
ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r10.anchor: وفي التفسير أنه نهاهم أن يحذفوا الدراهم.

ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r11.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r11.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r11.claim: One explanation is that they used praise ironically to mean that he was foolish and ignorant.
ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r11.anchor: قيل كنى بذا عن أنهم قالوا له:

ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r12.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r12.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r12.claim: Another view is that they said it mockingly.
ZAJJAJ:v3p72/r12.anchor: وقيل إنهم قالوا له هذا على وجه السخري

ASAD-NOTES:11:87#n120/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:87#n120/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:11:87#n120/r1.claim: Asad notes that the literal wording is plural: "Do thy prayers command thee?"
ASAD-NOTES:11:87#n120/r1.anchor: Lit., "Do thy prayers command thee...", etc.

ASAD-NOTES:11:87#n121/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:87#n121/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:11:87#n121/r1.claim: The people's desired freedom to use their wealth ignores others' rights and needs, especially those of the poor; this explains their sarcasm about Shu'ayb.
ASAD-NOTES:11:87#n121/r1.anchor: without regard to the rights and needs of others, especially the poor: hence their sarcastic reference, in the next sentence, to Shu'ayb's clemency and right-mindedness

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p34/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p34/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p34/r1.claim: She treats Qur'anic inimitability as an open field: generations build on earlier work, from al-Jahiz through al-Baqillani and later scholars, while no generation exhausts the Qur'an or says its final word.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p34/r1.anchor: ونبدأ نحن من حيث انتهى السلف، وتراثهم بين أيدينا علامات على الطريق، لا نغض من قيمته ولا نحط من أقدار أهله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p828/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p828/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p828/r1.claim: Calling Shu'ayb forbearing and rightly guided is ironic praise: his people mean the opposite, as in the taunt in 44:49; context reveals the mockery.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p828/r1.anchor: هو في الأصل مدح لكن إن وضعناه في سياق الآيات فهي استهزاء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.claim: Sibawayh raises the verb after حتى when it is detached from an asserted first action already completed; he uses the subjunctive when entry is intended as the endpoint.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.anchor: فإن جعلت الدخول في كل ذا غاية نصبت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.claim: He rejects the claim that the subjunctive follows merely because the speaker is uncertain; even an explicit uncertainty adjunct does not require it.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.anchor: ومن زعم أن النصب يكون في ذا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.claim: He criticizes grammarians who force the subjunctive to avoid a perceived inversion: Arabs still raise after قد سرت.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.claim: With negated or rare little travel, raising presents entry as separate, while the subjunctive makes it the endpoint; قلما can negate many trips or much travel in one trip.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.anchor: ما سرت حتى أدخلها وحتى أدخلها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.claim: Al-Khalil says إنما سرت حتى أدخلها is awkward unless the trip is belittled; the wording otherwise gives no sign that the travel ended before entry.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.anchor: وهذا قول الخليل | وتقول كان سيرى أمس

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.claim: The verb after حتى does not share the syntactic slot of the first verb as a verb after فاء does; it is detached like a clause after إذا or an introductory particle.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.anchor: واعلم أن ما بعد حتى لا يشرك الفعل الذي قبل حتى في موضعه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.claim: After a nonasserted clause, حتى takes only the subjunctive because it reverts to أن or كي instead of acting as a clause-initial connector.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.anchor: واعلم أن الفعل إذا كان غير

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.claim: أيهم سار حتى يدخلها allows raising because travel and entry are already asserted and only the actor is queried; أسرت حتى تدخلها requires subjunctive because no trip was affirmed.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.anchor: تقول أيهم سار حتى يدخلها لأنك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.claim: In some contexts the present نفعل can stand for past فعلنا; a Sululi poem illustrates this, and أسير likewise means سرت when intended as past.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.anchor: فعلنا في بعض المواضع ومثل ذلك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.claim: With كان, an adverb like أمس can complete the first clause and permit raising after حتى; without a predicate for كان, that analysis fails.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالرفعفيمااتصلبالأولكاتصا.anchor: وتقول كان سيرى أمس سيرا متعبا حتى أدخلها

NASHR:v1p451/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p451/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p451/r4.claim: Eight words with final hamza after alif are written with the hamza on waw without disagreement; the listed examples include شركاء in al-Anʿām, نشاء in Hūd, and دعاء in Ghāfir.
NASHR:v1p451/r4.anchor: فالمضمومة منها ثمان كلمات كتبت الهمزة فيها واوا بلا خلاف، وهي (شركاء) في الأنعام

NASHR:v2p290/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p290/r6.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص والباقون
NASHR:v2p290/r6.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, Khalaf, and Hafs read أصلاتك as a singular without wāw; the others retain wāw for the plural.
NASHR:v2p290/r6.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص بحذف الواو

NASHR:v1p38/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p38/r1.speaker: أبو العلاء الحسن بن أحمد بن الحسن الهمذاني
NASHR:v1p38/r1.claim: Al-Hamadhani introduces his work as a guide to the ten readers followed across the Hijaz, Syria, and Iraq.
NASHR:v1p38/r1.anchor: هذه تذكرة في اختلاف القراء العشرة الذين اقتدى الناس بقراءتهم

NASHR:v1p38/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p38/r2.speaker: ابن الصلاح
NASHR:v1p38/r2.claim: Ibn al-Salah requires a reading to be mass-transmitted from the Prophet, widespread, and accepted by the community; readings without certainty are forbidden, not merely disliked.
NASHR:v1p38/r2.anchor: قال شيخ الإسلام ومفتي الأنام العلامة أبو عمرو عثمان بن الصلاح - رحمه الله -

NASHR:v1p38/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p38/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p38/r3.claim: When al-Wasiti brought the ten readings to Damascus around 730 AH, a jealous local reciter sought to stop him through a judge.
NASHR:v1p38/r3.anchor: ولما قدم الشيخ أبو محمد عبد الله بن عبد المؤمن الواسطي دمشق في حدود سنة ثلاثين وسبعمائة

NASHR:v1p38/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p38/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p38/r4.claim: The scholars of that period agreed that teaching and reading the ten was permissible and that the ten readings form one sound body.
NASHR:v1p38/r4.anchor: لم يختلفوا في جواز ذلك واتفقوا على أن قراءات هؤلاء العشر واحدة

NASHR:v1p38/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p38/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p38/r5.claim: Scholars differed over calling readings beyond the ten anomalous; the author says any reading meeting the three established criteria is sound.
NASHR:v1p38/r5.anchor: اختلفوا في إطلاق الشاذ على ما عدا هؤلاء العشرة وتوقف بعضهم والصواب أن ما دخل في تلك الأركان الثلاثة فهو صحيح

NASHR:v1p38/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p38/r6.speaker: ابن تيمية
NASHR:v1p38/r6.claim: Ibn Taymiyya says the seven famous readers are not the seven revealed ahruf; Ibn Mujahid selected seven to match the number, not because they exhaust revelation or alone may be read.
NASHR:v1p38/r6.anchor: أبي العباس أحمد بن عبد الحليم بن عبد السلام بن تيمية - رحمه الله -: لا نزاع بين العلماء

NASHR:v1p38/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p38/r7.speaker: بعض أئمة القراء
NASHR:v1p38/r7.claim: An unnamed leading reader said he would have chosen Yaqub of Basra in place of Hamza had Ibn Mujahid not already selected Hamza.
NASHR:v1p38/r7.anchor: قال بعض من قال من أئمة القراء: لولا أن ابن مجاهد سبقني إلى حمزة لجعلت مكانه

NASHR:v1p38/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p38/r8.speaker: ابن تيمية
NASHR:v1p38/r8.claim: Ibn Taymiyya says established readings such as al-Aعمash’s or Yaqub’s may be read just as Hamza’s and al-Kisai’s may, without scholarly dispute.
NASHR:v1p38/r8.anchor: ولذلك لم يتنازع علماء الإسلام المتبعون من السلف والأئمة في أنه لا يتعين أن يقرأ بهذه القراءات المعينة

NASHR:v1p38/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p38/r9.speaker: ابن تيمية
NASHR:v1p38/r9.claim: Ibn Taymiyya reports that many senior imams who knew Hamza’s reading preferred the readings of the two Medinans Abu Jafar and Shayba and Basran teachers of Yaqub.
NASHR:v1p38/r9.anchor: بل أكثر العلماء الأئمة الذين أدركوا قراءة حمزة: كسفيان بن عيينة وأحمد بن حنبل وبشر

NASHR:v1p62/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p62/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p62/r1.claim: The author read the entire Quran according to the Shatibiyya with a succession of Egyptian Shafii reading masters, describing this as an exceptionally high and continuous transmission.
NASHR:v1p62/r1.anchor: وقرأت بمضمنها القرآن كله على جماعة من الشيوخ، منهم الشيخ الإمام العالم التقي

NASHR:v1p62/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p62/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p62/r2.claim: Although Shatibi’s son-in-law died before reciting the final al-Ahqaf narration of Abu al-Harith from al-Kisai, he had completed nineteen individual readings, combined readings, and received the Taysir readings by transmission and authorization; imams therefore count the full reading as received.
NASHR:v1p62/r2.anchor: إلا أن صهر الشاطبي بقي عليه من رواية أبي الحارث عن الكسائي من سورة الأحقاف

NASHR:v1p77#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p77#3/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p77#3/r1.claim: The excerpt identifies al-Talkhis as a work on eight readings by Abu Mashar al-Tabari, a Meccan reading master who died in 478 AH; the remainder is its transmission chain.
NASHR:v1p77#3/r1.anchor: في القراءات الثمان للإمام الأستاذ أبي معشر عبد الكريم بن عبد الصمد

NASHR:v1p490/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p490/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p490/r2.claim: The Bani Israel case has ten combinations from the five earlier methods with long or short easing of the second hamza; replacing hamza with ya to follow the script is anomalous, while deleting it is invalid.
NASHR:v1p490/r2.anchor: ومن ذلك (مسألة بني إسرائيل) وفيها بحكم ما ذكرنا عشرة أوجه وهي الخمسة المذكورة أولا

NASHR:v1p490/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p490/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p490/r3.claim: For “بما أنزل” the author lists three approaches: full realization, between-between easing through most Iraqi routes with long or short duration, and silence with full realization for the previously named routes.
NASHR:v1p490/r3.anchor: ومن ذلك (مسألة: بما أنزل) وفيها ثلاثة أوجه (الأول) التحقيق مذهب الجمهور

NASHR:v1p490/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p490/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p490/r4.claim: The combinations for “فلما أضاءت” total six after matching long with long and short with short; “كلما أضاء” reaches twelve when combined with three substitution options.
NASHR:v1p490/r4.anchor: وتجيء هذه الأربعة في نحو: (فلما أضاءت) مع تسهيل بالمد والقصر، فتصبح ستة

NASHR:v1p490/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p490/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p490/r5.claim: Combining the three options with the five final options in “ولا ابنا” produces eighteen valid faces after two conflicting combinations are removed.
NASHR:v1p490/r5.anchor: وتجيء الثلاثة أيضا مع الخمسة الأخيرة من قوله: (ولا ابنا) فتبلغ خمسة عشر وجها، بل عشرين

NASHR:v1p490/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p490/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p490/r6.claim: For “فسوف يأتيهم أنبؤا” and the analogous “شركاو” and “في أموالنا ما نشوا,” the excerpt counts twenty-four faces: twelve with silence on mīm and the listed combinations of substitution, duration, rawm, standard easing, script-following, sukun, and ishmaam.
NASHR:v1p490/r6.anchor: وفيه باعتبار ما تقدم في (شركاو، وفي أموالنا ما نشوا) أربعة وعشرون وجها وهي مع السكت على الميم اثنا عشر وجها

QIRAAT-ER:11:87:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:11:87:4#1/r1.speaker: Lvw|pl
QIRAAT-ER:11:87:4#1/r1.claim: The plural reading makes the mockery sharper by implying Shuaib's many prayers are what interfere and command them.
QIRAAT-ER:11:87:4#1/r1.anchor: Plural ṣalawāt: ""do your prayers (multiple) command you"" — pluralizing intensifies the mockery

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p311#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p311#2/r1.speaker: الأعمش
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p311#2/r1.anchor: عن الأعمش في قوله تعالى ﴿ أصلاتك تأمرك ﴾ قال أقراءتك

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r1.claim: They answer Shuʿayb's call to worship God alone, which entails rejecting idols, by denying that revelation commands him and insinuating delusion or madness.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r1.anchor: أجابوا بذلك أمره عليه السلام إياهم بعبادة الله تعالى وحده المتضمن لنهيهم عن عبادة الأصنام

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r2.claim: Their mocking question treats his prayer as a product of delusion and asks whether it can make them abandon the idols their ancestors worshiped for generations.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r3.claim: They portray Shuʿayb as commanded because he taught that his message came from revelation and was entrusted to him for delivery.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r3.anchor: وإنما جعلوه عليه السلام مأمورا مع أن الصادر عنه إنما هو الأمر بعبادة الله تعالى وغير ذلك من الشرائع لأنه عليه السلام لم يكن يأمرهم من تلقاء نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r4.speaker: الأحنف
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r4.claim: Al-Aḥnaf reports that Shuʿayb prayed more than the other prophets; his people winked and laughed when they saw him praying.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r4.anchor: أخرج ابن عساكر عن الأحنف أنه عليه السلام كان أكثر الأنبياء صلاة وكانوا إذا رأوه يصلي يتغامزون ويتضاحكون

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also explains the mockery by saying Shuʿayb used to tell them that prayer enjoins right and forbids indecency.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r5.anchor: إن الصلاة تأمر بالمعروف وتنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر وروي هذا عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r6.claim: Al-Alusi favors the explanation that Shuʿayb's conspicuous prayer made it a target of their mockery.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r6.anchor: وإلى الأول ذهب غير واحد وهذا الإسناد حقيقي لا مجازي

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r7.claim: The attribution of commanding to prayer is literal in their wording, although they intend it mockingly; the imperfect verb implies an ongoing command.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r7.anchor: وهذا الإسناد حقيقي لا مجازي غاية ما في الباب أنهم قصدوا الحقيقة تهكما واختيار المضارع ليدل على العموم بحسب الزمان

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r8.claim: One parse supplies تكليف before أن and treats the preposition as omitted, a regular construction; another says a person cannot be charged with another's act because it is beyond his power.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r8.anchor: على تقدير بتكليف أن نترك فحذف المضاف وهو تكليف

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r9.claim: An alternative without ellipsis has them mock Shuʿayb for supposedly ordering what lies outside his power or responsibility, but al-Alusi objects that the context gives no reason for such an order.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r9.anchor: وقيل : إن الداعي إليه أن الشخص لا يكلف بفعل غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r10.claim: They also answer his order to fulfill people's rights and stop shortchanging; أو coordinates with ما and means “and,” covering whatever they choose to do with their wealth.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r10.anchor: أجابوا به أمره عليه السلام بإيفاء الحقوق ونهيه عن البخس والنقص

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r11.claim: Coordinating the second clause with أن نترك would imply that Shuʿayb commanded their fraud, although he forbids it, so that parse is impossible.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r11.anchor: لاستحالة المعنى إذ يصير حينئذ تأمرك بفعلنا في أموالنا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r12.speaker: محمد بن كعب
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r12.claim: Muḥammad b. Kaʿb reports that they clipped dirhams and dinars and passed them off with sound coins to deceive buyers.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r12.anchor: وقيل : كانوا يقرضون الدراهم والدنانير ويجرونها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r13.claim: Some include that coin fraud in corruption on earth and thus in the verse's general wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r13.anchor: وأدخل بعضهم ذلك الفعل في العثي في الأرض فيكون النهي عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r14.speaker: أكثر السبعة
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r14.claim: Most of the Seven reciters read صلواتك in the plural; al-Alusi says the plural and singular readings are readily reconciled.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r14.anchor: وقرأ أكثر السبعة أصلواتك بالجمع وأمر الجمع بين القرائتين سهل

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r15.speaker: الضحاك بن قيس وابن أبي عبلة وزيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r15.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk b. Qays, Ibn Abī ʿAbla, and Zayd b. ʿAlī read both verbs in the second person, making the second clause depend on تأمرك: does your prayer command you to do as you wish with our wealth?
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r15.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك بن قيس وابن أبي عبلة وزيد بن علي بالتاء في الفعلين على الخطاب

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r16.claim: The apparent meaning of “what you wish” in the second-person reading is that Shuʿayb would require them to fulfill the measure and weight.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r16.anchor: أي من إيفاء المكيال والميزان كما هو الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r17.speaker: سفيان الثوري
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r17.claim: Another view takes it as almsgiving; Shuʿayb called them to give zakat, according to Sufyān al-Thawrī.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r17.anchor: وقيل : من الزكاة فقد كان عليه السلام يأمرهم بها كما روي عن سفيان الثوري

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r18.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r18.claim: Al-Ḥasan says every prophet was charged with prayer and almsgiving, but al-Alusi says this report does not establish the point here.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r18.anchor: عن الحسن أنه قال : لم يبعث الله تعالى نبيا إلا فرض عليه الصلاة والزكاة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r19.speaker: الأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r19.claim: Al-Aʿmash interprets صلاة here as recitation.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r19.anchor: ابن المنذر وغيره عن الأعمش تفسيرها بالقراءة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r20.speaker: غيره
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r20.claim: Other interpreters explain صلاة as supplication, its lexical sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r20.anchor: ونقل عن غيره تفسيرها بالدعاء الذي هو المعنى اللغوي لها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r21.speaker: أبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r21.claim: Abū Muslim takes صلاة to mean religion, one of its most important aspects.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r21.anchor: وعن أبي مسلم تفسيرها بالدين لأنها من أجل أموره

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r22.claim: Even if صلاة means ritual prayer, the verse proves only that Shuʿayb prayed, not that his community was required to do so; it may have been his special practice.
