ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r22.anchor: يمكن أن يكون ذلك من خصوصياته عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r23.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن وطلحة
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r23.claim: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Ṭalḥa read the first verb with ن and the second with ت, coordinating the second clause with the object of تأمرك.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p117/r23.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبدالرحمن وطلحة بالنون في الأول والتاء في الثاني والعطف

ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والمبرد
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and al-Mubarrad take “forbearing, prudent” as sarcastic irony meaning the opposites.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r1.anchor: فالمراد بهما ضد معناهما وهذا هو المروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما وإليه ذهب قتادة والمبرد

ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r2.claim: Alternatively, they call him forbearing and prudent according to their own claim, and use those traits to question why he would demand such change.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r2.anchor: وجوز أن يكونوا وصفوه بذلك بناءا على الزعم والجملة تعليل لما سبق من استبعاد ما ذكروه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r3.claim: The ironic reading best fits the preceding mockery; another preference for the literal reading compares their words with the people of Ṣāliḥ.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r3.anchor: ورجح الأول بأنه الأنسب بما قبله لأنه تهكم أيضا ورجح الأخير بأنه يكون الكلام عليه نظير ما مر في قصة صالح

ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r4.claim: The literal comparison recalls the people of Ṣāliḥ telling him that they had previously placed their hopes in him, before Shuʿayb responds in the next verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r4.anchor: وتعقيبه بمثل ما عقب به ذلك حسبما تضمنه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r1.speaker: أبو مسلم وعطاء
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r1.claim: Shaykh al-Islam says the proposed conditional readings fit only if the mockers meant religion by صلاة, as Abū Muslim and ʿAṭāʾ reportedly do.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r1.anchor: إن حمل كلامهم على الحقيقة وأريد بالصلاة الدين حسبما نقل عن أبي مسلم وعطاء

ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r5.claim: He rejects the claim that the conditional answer requires treating the mockers' words literally or taking صلاة to mean religion; the answer works with their taunt and the ordinary sense of prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r5.anchor: ليس في الكلام ما يأبى عنه ولا يتوقف على حمل الكلام على الحقيقة والصلاة على الدين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r1.claim: The worship practiced by their ancestors refers to idols.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r1.anchor: قالوا يا شعيب أصلاتك تأمرك أن نترك ما يعبد آباؤنا} من الأوثان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Shuʿayb prayed often, prompting their remark about his prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: كان شعيب عليه السلام كثير الصلاة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r3.speaker: الأعمش
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r3.claim: Al-Aʿmash interprets the word as your recitation.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r4.claim: Their claim about doing as they wished with their wealth includes increasing and decreasing it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r4.anchor: {أو أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء} من الزيادة والنقصان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r5.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r5.claim: Another report says Shuʿayb forbade clipping dinars and dirhams, calling it unlawful, and they objected that they could do as they wished with their money.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: كان شعيب عليه السلام نهاهم عن قطع الدنانير والدراهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they meant the opposites, foolish and misguided; Arabs may name something by its opposite, as in calling a bitten person sound or a desert a salvation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: أرادوا: السفيه الغاوي، والعرب تصف الشيء بضده

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r7.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r7.claim: Another view takes their words as mockery.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r8.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r8.claim: Another explanation is that they called him forbearing and right-guided according to his own claim.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r9.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r9.claim: A literal reading has them call Shuʿayb forbearing and right-guided among his people and argue he should not divide them by opposing their religion; they use the same reproach made to Ṣāliḥ in 11:62.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p195#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: هو على الصحة أي إنك يا شعيب فينا حليم رشيد، لا يجمل بك شق عصا قومك

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r1.claim: They mock his monotheistic message and prayer, suggesting his call has no rational motive and comes from the fancies of someone devoted to prayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r1.anchor: على الاستهزاء به والتهكم بصلواته والإشعار بأن مثله

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r2.claim: Shuʿayb prayed frequently, explaining why they used the plural and singled prayer out for mockery.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r2.anchor: وكان شعيب كثير الصلاة فلذلك جمعوا وخصوا الصلاة بالذكر

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r3.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ read “your prayer” in the singular.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص على الإفراد

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r4.claim: With the singular reading, the prayer commands them to leave; a genitive noun is omitted because a man does not command another’s action.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r4.anchor: فحذف المضاف لأن الرجل لا يؤمر بفعل غيره

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r5.claim: The phrase may coordinate with their ancestors’ worship, meaning “or leave doing as we wish with wealth”; a tāʾ reading coordinates with “that we leave” and answers the prohibition on cheating and command to give full measure.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r5.anchor: عطف على ما أي وأن نترك فعلنا ما نشاء في أموالنا

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r6.claim: A variant uses tāʾ in both verbs, coordinating with “that we leave” as the response to the ban on cheating and the command to give full measure.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r6.anchor: بالتاء فيهما على أن العطف على { أن نترك }

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r7.claim: Some say Shuʿayb forbade clipping dirhams and dinars, which is what they meant by freedom with their money.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r7.anchor: كان ينهاهم عن تقطيع الدراهم والدنانير فأرادوا به ذلك

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r8.claim: They sarcastically describe him as the opposite of forbearing and rightly guided, or claim his good sense should restrain such exhortations.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:87/r8.anchor: تهكموا به وقصدوا وصفه بضد ذلك

BINTSHATI:v1p13/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p13/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p13/r1.claim: Arabic literary study has long selected poetry and prose as models while neglecting the Qur’an, the greatest Arabic book and its enduring rhetorical miracle and model of expression.

BINTSHATI:v1p13/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p13/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p13/r2.claim: University Arabic departments leave the Qur’an to tafsīr courses, with few attempts to bring it into rhetorical study alongside Arabic literary heritage.
BINTSHATI:v1p13/r2.anchor: ونحن في الجامعة، نترك هذا الكنز الغالي لدرس التفسير

BINTSHATI:v1p13/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p13/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p13/r3.claim: Until roughly a quarter-century before writing, tafsīr teaching generally followed a traditional transmitted approach focused on understanding the text as earlier exegetes did.
BINTSHATI:v1p13/r3.anchor: وكان المنهج المتبع في درس التفسير - إلى نحو ربع قرن من الزمان - تقليديا أثريا

BINTSHATI:v1p13/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p13/r4.speaker: أمين الخولي
BINTSHATI:v1p13/r4.claim: Amin al-Khūlī broke from the traditional pattern by treating the Qur’an as a linguistic and rhetorical text according to a method he established; the author was among his students.
BINTSHATI:v1p13/r4.anchor: حتى جاء شيخنا الإمام "الأستاذ أمين الخولي" فخرج به

BINTSHATI:v1p13/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p13/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p13/r5.claim: Literary tafsīr remained confined to tafsīr courses rather than entering the broader study of Arabic rhetoric and its heritage.
BINTSHATI:v1p13/r5.anchor: ولكن التفسير الأدبي للقرآن ظل حتى اليوم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p565/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p565/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p565/r7.claim: They call Shuʿayb by name rather than kinship, with rudeness and harshness, and mock the influence of his prayer.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p565/r7.anchor: سموه باسمه جفاء وغلظة وأنكروا عليه مستهزئين بصلاته

BIQAI-FULL:v3p565/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p565/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p565/r8.claim: They sarcastically portray his prayer as a constant commander telling them to abandon their fathers’ worship and stop doing whatever they want with their wealth.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p565/r8.anchor: تفعل معك فعل من كان يأمر دائما بتكليفنا

BIQAI-FULL:v3p565/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p565/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p565/r9.claim: They describe fraud, ruined transactions, gambling, and similar practices as doing with money whatever they please, and suppose restraint would squander wealth.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p565/r9.anchor: من قطع الدهم والدينار وإفساد المعاملة والمقامرة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p565/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p565/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p565/r10.claim: Biqaʿi traces the forms of ṣalā to connection: prayer joins servant and Lord, while supplication, seeking pardon, and Jewish synagogues also express connection; he promises a fuller account at 13:15.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p565/r10.anchor: ومادة صلا - واوية ويائية مهموزة وغير مهموزة بجميع تقاليبها - تدور على الوصلة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r1.claim: The people use ḥalīm and rashīd sarcastically, twisting the virtues into alleged patience with what relatives dislike and foolishness about money.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r1.anchor: يريدون بهذا كما زعموا - سلخه من كل ما هو متصف به دونهم من هاتين الصفتين الفائقتين

BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r2.claim: Their taunt is meant to accuse Shuʿayb of folly and error by mockery.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r2.anchor: وعنوا بذلك نسبته إلى السفه والغي على طريق التهكم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r3.claim: Their appeal to their fathers rests on blind imitation and the presumption that ancestral practice cannot be wrong.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r3.anchor: فدارت شبهتهم في الأمرين على تلقيد الآباء

DURR-FULL:v4p465/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r9.speaker: الأعمش
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r9.anchor: عن الأعمش رضي الله عنه في قوله {أصلاتك تأمرك} قال: أقراءتك

DURR-FULL:v4p465/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r10.speaker: الأحنف
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r10.claim: Al-Ahnaf reports that Shuʿayb prayed more than the other prophets.
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r10.anchor: عن الأحنف رضي الله عنه أن شعيبا كان أكثر الأنبياء صلاة

DURR-FULL:v4p465/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd says Shuʿayb forbade clipping coins; his people objected that they could cut, burn, or discard their own money.
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r11.anchor:
عن ابن زيد رضي الله عنه في قوله {يا شعيب أصلاتك تأمرك} الآية
قال: نهاهم عن قطع هذه الدنانير والدراهم

DURR-FULL:v4p465/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r12.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r12.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says Shuʿayb’s people were punished for clipping dirhams.
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r12.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي رضي الله عنه قال: عذب قوم شعيب في قطعهم الدراهم وهو قوله {أو أن نفعل في أموالنا

DURR-FULL:v4p465/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r13.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r13.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam identifies their claimed freedom with clipping dirhams and calls it corruption on earth.
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r13.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم رضي الله عنه {أو أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء} قال: قرض الدراهم وهو من الفساد في الأرض

DURR-FULL:v4p465/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r14.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r14.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib defines clipped coins as recognized circulating weights and classifies clipping them as corruption.
DURR-FULL:v4p465/r14.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب رضي الله عنه قال: قطع الدراهم والدنانير المثاقيل التي قد جازت بين الناس وعرفوها من الفساد في الأرض

DURR-FULL:v4p467/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r1.speaker: ربيعة بن أبي هلال
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r1.claim: Rabiʿa ibn Abi Hilal reports that Ibn al-Zubayr punished someone for clipping a dirham.
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r1.anchor: عن ربيعة بن أبي هلال أن ابن الزبير عاقب في قرض الدرهم

DURR-FULL:v4p467/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says their praise meant the opposite: that Shuʿayb was neither forbearing nor rightly guided.

DURR-FULL:v4p467/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r3.claim: Qatada says the description was uttered mockingly.
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r3.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {إنك لأنت الحليم الرشيد} استهزاء به

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r1.speaker: الأعمش
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r1.claim: Al-A'mash glosses your prayers as your recitation.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says Shuayb's prayers really did command his people to abandon what their forefathers worshiped.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r2.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : يا شعيب اصلاتك تامرك ان نترك ما يعبد اباؤنا يقول

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says they were forbidden to shave small amounts off coins, which he calls corruption in the land.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r3.anchor: عن زيد ابن اسلم أو ان نفعل في اموالنا مانشاء قال : كان ينهاهم عن حذف الدراهم وحذف الدراهم من الفساد في الأرض

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r4.claim: Qatada glosses the phrase as doing whatever they desire.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة أو ان نفعل في اموالنا مانشاء اي : مانشتهي

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r5.speaker: سفيان الثوري
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r5.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri says the phrase refers to zakat.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r5.anchor: ثنا سفيان الثوري في قوله : أو ان نفعل في اموالنا مانشاء قال : الزكاة

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the people meant the opposite of the words, mocking Shuayb as neither forbearing nor rightly guided.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قول قوم شعيب : انك لانت الحليم الرشيد قال : يقولون : انك لست بحليم ولا برشيد

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r7.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r7.claim: Maymun ibn Mihran says the phrase was spoken in mockery.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r7.anchor: عن ميمون بن مهران في قول الله : انك لانت الحليم الرشيد قال : هزوا

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r8.claim: Qatada says the people were mocking the Prophet.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2072#2/r8.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : انك لانت الحليم الرشيد قال : استهزاء بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143/r1.claim: Their address is another sarcastic remark, sharpened by four emphases: إن, the oath lām, and the restrictive force of لأنت.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143/r1.anchor: وبصيغة القصر في جملة { لأنت الحليم الرشيد } فاشتملت على أربعة مؤكدات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143/r2.claim: For the added sarcasm, al-halim means intelligent or rational, while al-rashid means sound in managing money.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143/r2.anchor: زيادة في التهكم : ذو الحلم أي العقل ، والرشيد : الحسن التدبير في المال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r1.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r1.claim: The majority read ‘your prayers’ in the plural, while Ibn Waththab reads it in the singular; he likewise uses the singular in the cited verses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r1.anchor: قرأ جمهور الناس «أصلواتك» بالجمع، وقرأ ابن وثاب «أصلاتك» بالإفراد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r2.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r2.claim: One group understands Shuayb’s prayer as the familiar prescribed prayers; a report says he was the most prayerful of the prophets.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r2.anchor: فقالت فرقة: أرادوا الصلوات المعروفة، وروي أن شعيبا عليه السلام كان أكثر الأنبياء صلاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r3.claim: Hasan says God imposed prayer and almsgiving on every prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: لم يبعث الله نبيا إلا فرض عليه الصلاة والزكاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r4.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r4.claim: Other interpretations take ‘your prayers’ to mean Shuayb’s recitation, his mosques, or his supplications.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r4.anchor: وقيل: أرادوا قراءتك. وقيل أرادوا: أمساجدك؟ وقيل: أرادوا: أدعواتك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya finds the prescribed prayers and supplications likeliest: their rank in prayer is represented as urging Shuayb to denounce their religion and customs, as prayer restrains indecency.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r5.anchor: وأقرب هذه الأقوال الأول والرابع وجعلوا الأمر من فعل الصلوات على جهة التجوز

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r6.claim: Their complaint explicitly shows that their ancestors worshipped gods other than God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200/r6.anchor: وقوله: أن نترك ما يعبد آباؤنا نص في أنهم كانوا يعبدون غير الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r1.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r1.claim: The majority read both verbs with first-person plural nūn. Al-Dahhak reads both with second-person tāʾ; Abu Abd al-Rahman reports nūn then tāʾ, as does Ibn Abbas.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك بن قيس «تفعل» و «تشاء» بتاء المخاطبة فيهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r2.claim: With nūn in both verbs, the second ‘an’ coordinates with ‘what,’ not the first ‘an’; otherwise the sense becomes ‘Does your prayer command us to do whatever we wish with our property?’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r2.anchor: فأما من قرأ بالنون فيهما ف أن الثانية عطف على ما لا على أن الأولى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r3.speaker: بعض النحويين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r3.claim: Some grammarians allow the second ‘an’ in the tāʾ reading to coordinate with ‘what’; they also allow coordination to the first ‘an’.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r3.anchor: قال بعض النحويين، ويصح عطفها على ما ويتم المعنى في الوجهين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya objects that ‘leave’ means ‘abandon’ in the first clause but ‘allow’ in the second, so the parsing requires semantic variation or an omitted noun; nūn-then-tāʾ cannot coordinate the second ‘an’ with ‘what’ without reversing the sense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r4.anchor: ويجيء نترك في الأول بمعنى نرفض، وفي الثاني بمعنى نقرر، فيتعذر عندي هذا الوجه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r5.claim: The apparent reference to what they do with their property is the short measure and weight already mentioned.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r5.anchor: وظاهر فعلهم هذا الذي أشاروا إليه هو بخس الكيل والوزن الذي تقدم ذكره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb and others say the phrase alludes to clipping dirhams and dinars and fraudulently passing them alongside genuine coins.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r6.anchor: وروي أن الإشارة هي إلى قرضهم الدينار والدرهم وإجراء ذلك مع الصحيح على جهة التدليس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r7.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r7.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab calls clipping coins corruption in the land; this is interpreted as the fraud described or changing coinage to consume people’s wealth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r7.anchor: وروي عن سعيد بن المسيب أنه قال: قطع الدراهم والدنانير من الفساد في الأرض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r8.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r8.claim: One interpretation is that they actually called Shuayb ignorant and foolish, while God veiled their insult with the opposite wording.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r8.anchor: فقيل: إنما كانت ألفاظهم: إنك لأنت الجاهل السفيه، فكنى الله عن ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r9.speaker: ابن جريج وابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r9.claim: Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd say these were their exact words, spoken sarcastically.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r9.anchor: إلا أنهم قالوه على جهة الاستهزاء- قاله ابن جريج وابن زيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r10.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r10.claim: Another view has them mean that Shuayb is forbearing and rightly guided only in his own estimation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r10.anchor: وقيل المعنى: إنك لأنت الحليم الرشيد عند نفسك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r11.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r11.claim: A further view takes the praise literally as their belief, then makes it a rebuke: a truly wise man should not issue such commands.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r11.anchor: وقيل: بل قالوه على جهة الحقيقة وأنه اعتقادهم فيه، فكأنهم فندوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r12.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r12.claim: A report says that when the Prophet addressed Banu Qurayza as ‘brothers of apes,’ they replied, ‘Muhammad, we never knew you to be ignorant.’ Ibn Atiyya compares the gentleness of Shuayb’s speech with Muhammad’s address.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p200#2/r12.anchor: حين قال لهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «يا إخوة القردة» ، يا محمد ما علمناك جهولا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r1.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf, and Ḥafṣ read ṣalātuka in the singular.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r1.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص أصلاتك على التوحيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r2.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r2.claim: ʿAṭāʾ interprets Shuʿayb's ṣalāt as his religion.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r3.speaker: الأعمش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r3.claim: Al-Aʿmash interprets it as Shuʿayb's recitation.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r4.claim: A third view takes it as the familiar ritual prayers, noting that Shuʿayb prayed often.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r4.anchor: والثالث أنها الصلوات المعروفة وكان شعيب كثير الصلاة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r5.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ construes the question as asking whether Shuʿayb's prayers command them to abandon ancestral worship or to abandon doing as they wish with their wealth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r5.anchor: قال الفراء معنى الآية أصلواتك تأمرك أن نترك ما يعبد آباؤنا أو أن نترك أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says their conduct with their wealth was fraud and short measure, which they regarded as mutually agreed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r6.anchor: أحدهما أن فعلهم في أموالهم هو البخس والتطفيف قاله ابن عباس فالمعنى قد تراضينا فيما بيننا بذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says they cut dirhams and dinars.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r7.anchor: والثاني أنهم كانوا يقطعون الدراهم والدنانير فنهاهم عن ذلك قاله ابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r8.speaker: القرظي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r8.claim: Al-Quraẓī reports that they were punished for clipping dirhams.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r8.anchor: وقال القرظي عذبوا في قطعهم الدارهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r9.speaker: الضحاك بن قيس الفهري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r9.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays al-Fihrī reads the verb in the second person, mā tashāʾ, and coordinates it with an tatruka without ellipsis.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r9.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك بن قيس الفهري ما تشاء بالتاء ونسق أن تفعل على أن تترك واستغنى عن الإضمار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r10.speaker: سفيان الثوري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r10.claim: Sufyān al-Thawrī says this reading means Shuʿayb ordered them to give zakāt and they refused.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r10.anchor: قال سفيان الثوري في معنى هذه القراءة أنه أمرهم بالزكاة فامتنعوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r11.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي والضحاك وابن أبي عبلة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r11.claim: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read both verbs in the second person, with the same meaning as al-Fihrī's reading.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r11.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي والضحاك وابن أبي عبلة أو أن تفعل في أموالنا ما تشاء بالتاء فيهما ومعنى هذه القراءة كمعنى قراءة الفهري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r12.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس وقتادة والفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r12.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and al-Farrāʾ say the people spoke sarcastically.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r12.anchor: أحدها أنهم قالوه استهزاء به رواه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس وبه قال قتادة والفراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r13.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r13.claim: Al-Zajjāj says they used the phrase ironically to call Shuʿayb foolish and ignorant.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r13.anchor: والثاني أنهم قالوا له إنك لأنت السفيه الجاهل فكنى بهذا عن ذلك ذكره الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r14.speaker: أبو الحسن المصيصي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r14.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Muṣīṣī says they insulted Shuʿayb as neither forbearing nor rightly guided, while God affirms that he truly is both.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r14.anchor: والثالث أنهم سبوه بأنه ليس بحليم ولا رشيد فأثنى الله عز وجل عليه فقال بل إنك لأنت الحليم الرشيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r15.speaker: الماوردي وابن كيسان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r15.claim: Al-Māwardī and Ibn Kaysān say they sincerely acknowledged Shuʿayb's forbearance and sound guidance, then challenged his authority over their property.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p149/r15.anchor: والرابع أنهم اعترفوا له بالحلم والرشد حقيقة وقالوا أنت حليم رشيد فلم تنهانا أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r1.claim: The Qur'an honors the community, guides people by God's enabling, reforms them through promise and warning, and is protected from ignorant alteration and hostile distortion.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r1.anchor: القرآن المجيد ودعانا بتوفيقه على الحكم إلى الأمر الرشيد وقوم به نفوسنا بين الوعد والوعيد وحفظه من تغيير الجهول وتحريف العنيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r2.claim: The Qur'an's challenge to all humans and jinn to produce its like is cited at 17:88.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r2.anchor: فقال ﴿ قل لئن اجتمعت الإنس والجن على أن يأتوا بمثل هذا القرآن لا يأتون بمثله ولو كان بعضهم لبعض ظهيرا ﴾ الاسراء 88

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r3.claim: Muhammad was sent to people near and far as bearer of good tidings and warning, a shining lamp, and recipient of abundant favor; he has no equal among his kind.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r3.anchor: أرسله إلى القريب والبعيد بشيرا للخلائق ونذيرا وسراجا فى الأكوان منيرا ووهب له من فضله خيرا كثيرا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r4.claim: The Qur'an is the noblest field of knowledge, so understanding its meanings is the highest form of understanding; the worth of knowledge follows the worth of its subject.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r4.anchor: لما كان القرأن العزيز أشرف العلوم كان الفهم لمعانيه أوفى الفهوم لأن شرف العلم بشرف المعلوم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r5.claim: Ibn al-Jawzī found large tafsirs inaccessible, short ones incomplete, and medium works disorganized and often inattentive to difficult passages.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r5.anchor: فوجدتها بين كبير قد يئس الحافظ منه وصغير لا يستفاد كل المقصود منه والمتوسط منها قليل الفوائد عديم الترتيب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r6.claim: He wrote this concise tafsir to contain substantial knowledge, compressed its wording, and urges the reader to memorize it, seeking God's help.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r6.anchor: فأتيتك بهذا المختصر اليسير منظويا على العلم الغزير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the Companions learned ten verses from the Messenger at a time and did not move on until they understood their knowledge and practice.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r7.anchor: روى أبو عبد الرحمن السلمى عن ابن مسعود قال كنا نتعلم من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم العشر فلا نجاوزها إلى العشر الآخر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r8.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan, transmitted by Qatāda, said he wanted to know the occasion and intended meaning of every verse God revealed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p3/r8.anchor: وروى قتادة عن الحسن أنه قال ما أنزل الله آية إلا أحب أن أعلم فيم أنزلت وماذا عنى بها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r1.speaker: الأعمش
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r1.claim: Al-A'mash explains the taunting question about Shu'ayb's prayer as referring to his Qur'an.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r1.anchor: قال الأعمش: أي: قرآنك (7) {تأمرك أن نترك ما يعبد آباؤنا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r2.claim: What their fathers worship means idols and images.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r3.claim: Hasan says yes, Shu'ayb's prayer truly commands them to abandon what their fathers worshipped.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r3.anchor: قال الحسن] (9) في قوله: {أصلاتك تأمرك أن نترك ما يعبد آباؤنا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r4.speaker: الثوري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r4.claim: Al-Thawri interprets the people's claim that they may do as they wish with their wealth as referring to zakah.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r4.anchor: وقال الثوري في قوله: {أو أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء} يعنون الزكاة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r5.claim: In their mocking response, Shu'ayb's people claim their wealth is theirs to use as they wish and reject his demand to stop cheating in measure.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r5.anchor: على قولك، هي أموالنا نفعل فيها ما نريد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، وميمون بن مهران، وابن جريج، وابن أسلم، وابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas, Maymun ibn Mihran, Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Aslam, and Ibn Jarir say the enemies call Shu'ayb clement and rightly guided sarcastically.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p343#3/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وميمون بن مهران، وابن جريج، وابن أسلم، وابن جرير: يقولون ذلك -أعداء الله -على سبيل الاستهزاء

JISHUMI:v5p3551/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3551/r1.speaker: حمزة، والكسائي، وحفص عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v5p3551/r1.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs from Asim read the singular صلاة without waw, while the others read the plural صلوات.
JISHUMI:v5p3551/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة، والكسائي، وحفص عن عاصم: أصلاتك بغير واو على الجنس، وقرأ الباقون: صلواتك بالواو على الجمع.

JISHUMI:v5p3551/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3551/r2.speaker: بعضهم
JISHUMI:v5p3551/r2.claim: The common reading has the speakers say we do what we wish; some read both verbs with ta, meaning Shu'ayb commands what they do with their wealth, a construction the author says is more apt but not to be read in both forms.
JISHUMI:v5p3551/r2.anchor: قراءة العامة: نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء بالنون

JISHUMI:v5p3551/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3551/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3551/r7.claim: The phrase is not coordinated with the first أن; it coordinates with ما, yielding the sense of leaving them free to act in their wealth as they wish.
JISHUMI:v5p3551/r7.anchor: ليس بعطف على (أن) الأولى، وإنما هو معطوف على (ما) بتقدير: أو نترك فعل ما نشاء في أموالنا

JISHUMI:v5p3551/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3551/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3551/r8.claim: An alternative parse treats the command as a prohibition: the people ask whether prayer commands one thing and forbids another, returning the coordination to the first أن.
JISHUMI:v5p3551/r8.anchor: وفيه وجه آخر، أن يجعل الأمر كالنهي، كأنه قيل: أصلواتك تأمرك بكذا، وتنهاك عن كذا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r1.claim: Shuʿayb prayed often; when his people saw him praying, they exchanged glances and laughed, so their question mocks his worship.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r1.anchor: كان شعيب عليه السلام كثير الصلوات ، وكان قومه إذا رأوه يصلي تغامزوا وتضاحكوا ،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r2.claim: Prayer can metaphorically command or forbid good, as in 29:45, but the people deliberately cast it as a ridiculous command to ridicule Shuʿayb's prayer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r2.anchor: وإن جاز أن تكون آمرة على طريق المجاز ، كما كانت ناهية في قوله : { اتل ما أوحى إليك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r3.claim: They imply that abandoning idols has no rational basis and must come from delirium or satanic obsession, which they associate with his constant prayers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r3.anchor: فلم يبق إلا أن يأمرك به آمر هذيان ووسوسة شيطان ، وهو صلواتك التي تداوم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r4.claim: The construction means your prayer commands us with the charge to abandon ancestral worship; التكليف is elided because one person is not commanded to perform another's act.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r4.anchor: ومعنى تأمرك { أن نترك } تأمرك بتكليف أن نترك { ما يعبد ءاباؤنا }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r5.claim: A variant reads the word in the singular, أصلاتك.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r6.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads both verbs with direct address: أو أن تفعل في أموالنا ما تشاء, referring to Shuʿayb's prohibition of fraud and counsel to accept lawful earnings.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة ( أو أن تفعل في أموالنا ما تشاء ) بتاء الخطاب فيهما ،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r7.claim: Shuʿayb urged them to stop shortchanging and accept a small lawful gain rather than a large forbidden one; another report says he forbade clipping coins.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r7.anchor: وهو ما كان يأمرهم به من ترك التطفيف والبخس ، والاقتناع بالحلال القليل من الحرام الكثير .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r8.claim: They ironically call Shuʿayb supremely foolish and astray, reversing praise as one might sarcastically call a miser Hatim.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r8.anchor: نسبته إلى غاية السفه والغي ، فعكسوا ليتهكموا به ، كما يتهكم بالشحيح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r9.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r9.claim: Alternatively, they say he is reputed among his people for patience and right guidance, implying his commands contradict that reputation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p395#2/r9.anchor: وقيل : معناه إنك للمتواصف بالحلم والرشد في قومك ، يعنون أن ما تأمر به

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r2.claim: It may mean Shuʿayb’s devotional prayer to God.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r3.claim: It may mean his religion, which he was ordered to follow; ṣalāt’s root sense is following, as in the horse-racing term al-muṣallī.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r3.anchor: دينك الذي تدين به وأمرت باتباعه لأن أصل الصلاة الاتباع , ومنه أخذ المصلي في الخيل

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r4.claim: The question can mean that Shuʿayb’s prayer calls him to their way.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r5.claim: Alternatively, the question asks whether his prayer commands them to abandon the idols and images their ancestors worshipped.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r5.anchor: فيها أن تأمرنا أن نترك ما يعبد آباؤنا يعني من الأوثان والأصنام

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r6.claim: One explanation is that their desired conduct was cheating in weights and measures.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r6.anchor: ما كانوا عليه من البخس والتطفيف

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r7.speaker: زيد بن أسلم وسفيان الثوري
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r7.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam and Sufyān al-Thawrī say Shuʿayb commanded them to pay zakat, which they refused.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r7.anchor: الزكاة , كان يأمرهم بها فيمتنعون منها , قاله زيد بن أسلم وسفيان الثوري

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r8.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r8.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says Shuʿayb also forbade them from clipping coins.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r8.anchor: قطع الدراهم والدنانير لأنه كان ينهاهم عنه , قال زيد بن أسلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r9.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r9.claim: Qatāda says they called him wise and rightly guided sarcastically.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r9.anchor: قالوا ذلك استهزاء به , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads the words as a denial: they mean Shuʿayb is neither forbearing nor rightly guided.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r10.anchor: معناه أنك لست بحليم ولا رشيد على وجه النفي , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r11.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r11.claim: Ibn Baḥr says they sincerely concede Shuʿayb’s wisdom, then ask why he forbids them their desired conduct with their property.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p496/r11.anchor: اعترفوا له بالحلم والرشد على وجه والحقيقة وقالوا أنت حليم رشيد

MUQATIL:11:86-88/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:86-88/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:86-88/r3.claim: The people mock Shuayb, asking if his prayers command them to abandon the idols their fathers worshipped.
MUQATIL:11:86-88/r3.anchor: أصلواتك تأمرك أن نترك } ، يعني أن نعتزل

MUQATIL:11:86-88/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:86-88/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:86-88/r4.claim: They claim they may do as they wish with their money, either reducing measures and weights or giving full measure.
MUQATIL:11:86-88/r4.anchor: أو أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء } ، يعنون إن شئنا نقصنا

MUQATIL:11:86-88/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:86-88/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:86-88/r5.claim: In mockery, they call Shuayb a fool by saying patient and rightly guided, meaning foolish and astray.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p167#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167#4/r1.claim: Kufans other than Abū Bakr read the word as singular ṣalāt.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p167#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167#4/r2.claim: Shuaib prayed often and said prayer commands good and forbids wrong; his people mock the idea that prayer orders them to abandon ancestral worship and unrestricted financial dealings.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167#4/r2.anchor: كان شعيب عليه السلام كثير الصلوات وكان قومه يقولون له ما تستفيد بهذا فكان يقول إنها تامر بالمحاسن وتنهى عن القبائح

NASAFI-FULL:v2p167#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167#4/r3.claim: Their desired freedom with wealth includes either paying in full or shorting measure and weight.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p167#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167#4/r4.claim: Prayer is metaphorically called a commander, just as God calls it a forbidding force.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167#4/r4.anchor: وجاز أن تكون الصلوات آمرة مجازا كما سماها الله تعالى ناهية مجازا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p167#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167#4/r5.claim: Their description is ironic reversal meaning foolish and astray, or sincere acknowledgment that he is restrained and guided despite their refusal.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p167#4/r5.anchor: أى السفيه الضال وهذه تسمية على القلب استهزاء أو انك حليم رشيد عندنا ولست تفعل بنا ما يقتضيه حالك

QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r3.claim: A recitation has ṣalāt in the singular rather than ṣalawāt in the plural.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r4.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r4.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says أن is in the genitive, with the preposition bi understood.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r4.anchor: قال الكسائي: موضعها خفض على إضمار الباء

QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r5.claim: Shuʿayb was constant in obligatory and voluntary prayer and taught that prayer restrains indecency; his opponents mocked his devotion when he commanded and forbade them.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r5.anchor: أن شعيبا عليه السلام كان كثير الصلاة، مواظبا على العبادة فرضها ونفلها

QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r6.speaker: سفيان عن الأعمش
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r6.claim: Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, says prayer here means recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r6.anchor: قاله سفيان عن الأعمش، أي قراءتك تأمرك ودل بهذا على أنهم كانوا كفارا

QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r7.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan says God prescribed prayer and almsgiving for every prophet He sent.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن: لم يبعث الله نبيا إلا فرض عليه الصلاة والزكاة

QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r8.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ supplies an omitted verb: do you forbid us from doing whatever we want with our property?
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r8.anchor: زعم الفراء أن التقدير: أو تنهانا أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء

QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r9.speaker: السلمي والضحاك بن قيس
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r9.claim: Al-Sulamī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays read both verbs in the second person, asking what Shuʿayb wishes to do with their property.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r9.anchor: وقرأ السلمي والضحاك بن قيس «أو أن تفعل في أموالنا ما تشاء» بالتاء في الفعلين

QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r10.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r10.claim: On that reading, al-Naḥḥās says the second أن phrase coordinates with the first.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r10.anchor: وقال النحاس: «أو أن» على هذه القراءة معطوفة على «أن» الأولى

QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r11.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r11.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says one practice Shuʿayb forbade was clipping dirhams.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r11.anchor: وروي عن زيد بن أسلم أنه قال: كان مما نهاهم عنه حذف الدراهم

QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r12.claim: Another reading of their complaint is: if we mutually agree to cheat, why should Shuʿayb prevent it?
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r12.anchor: إذا تراضينا فيما بيننا بالبخس فلم تمنعنا منه؟

QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r13.claim: One view takes their praise as sarcastic, meaning Shuʿayb is forbearing and discerning only in his own estimation, like the taunt in 44:49.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r13.anchor: يعنون عند نفسك بزعمك ومثله في صفة أبي جهل

QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r14.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r14.claim: Qatāda says they said it in mockery and derision.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r14.anchor: قالوه على وجه الاستهزاء والسخرية، قاله قتادة

QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r15.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r15.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna says Arabs sometimes describe things by their opposites as an omen or hopeful euphemism, as with calling a stung person salīm.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r15.anchor: وقال سفيان بن عيينة: العرب تصف الشيء بضده للتطير والتفاؤل

QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r16.claim: Another interpretation takes the phrase as an insinuation intended as an insult.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r16.anchor: وقيل: هو تعريض أرادوا به السب

QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r17.claim: He prefers that they meant the praise sincerely: how could a truly forbearing, discerning man order them to abandon ancestral worship?
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r17.anchor: وأحسن من هذا كله، ويدل ما قبله على صحته، أي إنك أنت الحليم الرشيد حقا

QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r18.claim: Their reference to Shuʿayb's prayer shows they objected to a devout man, whom they considered wise, asking them to leave ancestral worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r18.anchor: أنكروا لما رأوا من كثرة صلاته وعبادته، وأنه حليم رشيد

QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r19.claim: He compares their expression with Jews of Qurayẓa telling the Prophet, after he called them brothers of apes, that they had not known him to be ignorant.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r19.anchor: ويشبه هذا المعنى قول اليهود من بني قريظة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حين قال لهم

QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r20.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r20.claim: Exegetes say they were punished for clipping the edges of sound coins, keeping the clippings, then trading intact coins by count and clipped coins by weight to cheat.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:86-88/r20.anchor: قال أهل التفسير: كان مما ينهاهم عنه، وعذبوا لأجله قطع الدنانير والدراهم

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r1.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r1.claim: Mālik says they broke dinars and dirhams; earlier exegetes including Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib and Zayd ibn Aslam say the same, and breaking them is a grave sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r1.anchor: قال ابن وهب قال مالك: كانوا يكسرون الدنانير والدراهم، وكذلك قال جماعة من المفسرين

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r2.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r2.claim: The Prophet prohibited breaking valid Muslim coinage except in necessity: intact coins retain their public value and benefit, while breaking them harms people.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r2.anchor: قال: نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن تكسر سكة المسلمين الجائزة بينهم إلا من بأس

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam interprets the nine corrupt men in 27:48 as coin breakers; Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr says Zayd was Madina's best Qur'an interpreter after Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r3.anchor: قاله زيد بن أسلم. قال أبو عمر بن عبد البر: زعموا أنه لم يكن بالمدينة أعلم بتأويل القرآن

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r4.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن القاسم
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r4.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim says a coin breaker is not a credible witness and ignorance is no excuse for this obvious offense.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r4.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن بن القاسم بن خالد بن جنادة مولى زيد بن الحارث العتقي: من كسرها لم تقبل شهادته

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r5.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r5.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī explains that a major sin removes probity; ignorance is no excuse for an obvious matter, though a truthful or genuinely obscured excuse can be accepted, as Mālik says.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r5.anchor: أما قوله: لم تقبل شهادته فلأنه أتى كبيرة، والكبائر تسقط العدالة دون الصغائر

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r6.claim: Since coin breaking is sinful corruption that invalidates testimony, its perpetrator should also be disciplined.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r6.anchor: إذا كان هذا معصية وفسادا ترد به الشهادة فإنه يعاقب من فعل ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r7.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r7.claim: Ibn al-Musayyib called coin clipping corruption on earth when he saw a man whipped for it, and did not object to the punishment; a similar view is related from Sufyān.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r7.anchor: ومر ابن المسيب برجل قد جلد فقال: ما هذا؟ قال رجل: يقطع الدنانير والدراهم

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r8.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r8.claim: As Madina's governor, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz whipped, shaved, and paraded a convicted clipper, saying he spared his hand only because he had not warned people earlier.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r8.anchor: وأمر فطيف به، وأمره أن يقول: هذا جزاء من يقطع الدراهم

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r9.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r9.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī accepts whipping and says shaving can remove an aid to sin; he considers removing any nonbodily means of sin obligatory.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r9.anchor: أما أدبه بالسوط فلا كلام فيه، وأما حلقه فقد فعله عمر

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r10.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r10.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī distinguishes clipping, which reduces coin value and secretly takes property, from breaking, which damages its form; ʿUmar may have analogized clipping to theft.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r10.anchor: وذلك أن قرض الدراهم غير كسرها، فإن الكسر إفساد الوصف، والقرض تنقيص للقدر

QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r11.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī answers that a coin's recognized function as dinar or dirham protects it; he notes that Ibn al-Zubayr also cut a clipper's hand.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:84-95/r11.anchor: حرز كل شيء على قدر حاله

QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r1.speaker: علماؤنا المالكية
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r1.claim: The Mālikī scholars call dinars and dirhams God's seals bearing His name; breaking God's seal deserves a different penalty from breaking a ruler's seal.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r1.anchor: قال علماؤنا المالكية: إن الدنانير والدراهم خواتيم الله عليها اسمه

QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r2.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r2.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī argues for amputation for clipping coins, says he applied it as a judge, and urges a righteous authority to do so for God.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r2.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وأرى أن يقطع في قرضها دون كسرها

BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r1.claim: They ask whether Shuʿayb's prayer commands them to abandon the idols worshipped by their forefathers.
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r1.anchor: أصلاتك تدعوك إلى أمرنا أن نترك ما يعبد آباؤنا من الأوثان

BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, they ask whether his prayer requires them to stop disposing of their property as they wish, answering his demand to fulfill rights and stop shortchanging.
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r2.anchor: أو أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشؤاه جواب عن أمره بإيفاء الحقوق ونهيه عن البخس والنقص

BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r3.claim: Here أو functions as و because Shuʿayb required both monotheism and fair dealing, not one choice between them.
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r3.anchor: وأو بمعنى الواو لأن ما كلفهم به شعيب هو مجموع الأمرين لاأحدهما.

BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r4.claim: The phrase means freely doing whatever transactions they wished with their property.
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r4.anchor: والمعنى أن نترك أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء من التصرفات

BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r5.claim: Some commentators say Shuʿayb specifically prohibited clipping the edges of dirhams and dinars, and this is what they meant by doing as they pleased with their money.
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم : كان ينهاهم عن تقطيع أطراف الدراهم والدنانير وقصها فأرادوا به ذلك.

BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r6.claim: The author says Shank first extracted iron, silver, and gold in Idris's era and was a righteous king who called people to Islam.
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r6.anchor: واعلم أن أول من استخرج الحديد والفضة والذهب من الأرض هو شنك في عصر إدريس عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r7.claim: The author attributes the first minting of the two precious metals to Dahhak and says any tampering with coinage is corruption on earth.
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r7.anchor: وأول من وضع السكة على النقدين الضحاك وإفساد السكة بأي وجه كان إفساد في الأرض

BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r8.claim: When asked what might save him, al-Hajjaj reportedly included that he had not corrupted people's currency.
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r8.anchor: وسئل الحجاج عما يرجو به النجاة فذكر أشياء منها ما أفسدت النقود على الناس

BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r9.speaker: الكواشي
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r9.claim: Al-Kawashi reads the words as saying Shuʿayb pretends to be forbearing and rightly guided, though he is not.
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r9.anchor: وقال في الكواشي : تتعاطى الحلم والرشد ولست كذلك ، أي : ما أنت بحليم ولا رشيد فيما تأمرنا وترشدنا إليه.

BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r10.speaker: أكثر أهل التفسير
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r10.claim: Most exegetes say they meant foolish, astray, and misguided, using الحليم الرشيد as a taunt.
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r10.anchor: وقال أكثر أهل التفسير : أرادوا السفيه الضال الغاوي فتهكموا به

BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r11.claim: The sarcasm borrows words for opposites: as one calls a miser generous or a fool wise, then transfers the ironic وصف to الحليم الرشيد.
BURSEVI:v4p109#2/r11.anchor: فهو إذا من قبيل الاستعارة التبيعة نزلوا التضاد منزلة التناسب على سبيل الهزؤ فاستعاروا الحلم والرشد للسفه والغواية ثم سرت الاستعارة منهما إلى الحليم الرشيد

RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r12.speaker: الباقون
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r12.claim: The remaining readers use the plural in the parallel Hūd phrase as well.
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r12.anchor: والباقون { صلواتك } وكذلك في هود على الجمع

RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r1.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Hafs from Asim read the word in the singular without wāw; the remaining readers read it plural with wāw.
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم { * أصلاتك } بغير واو . والباقون { ياشعيب أصلواتك } على الجمع

RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r2.claim: Shuʿayb had called them to monotheism and to abandon fraud; their reference to leaving their fathers’ worship answers the first demand, while their question about their money answers the second.
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r2.anchor: شعيبا عليه السلام أمرهم بشيئين ، بالتوحيد وترك البخس فالقوم أنكروا عليه أمره بهذين النوعين من الطاعة

RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r3.claim: Their appeal to their ancestors is adherence to inherited custom by sheer imitation.

RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r4.claim: One interpretation takes prayer as religion and faith, since it is religion’s most visible emblem; alternatively, its root evokes following, as the racehorse المصلي follows the leader, so the phrase means ‘your religion commands you.’
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r4.anchor: المراد منه الدين والإيمان ، لأن الصلاة أظهر شعار الدين فجعلوا ذكر الصلاة كناية عن الدين

RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r5.claim: Alternatively, they mean the formal prayers: Shuʿayb prayed often, and his people sarcastically mocked him when they saw him praying, as one might mock someone who attributes foolish speech to his reading.
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r5.anchor: أن المراد منه هذه الأعمال المخصوصة ، روي أن شعيبا كان كثير الصلاة وكان قومه إذا رأوه يصلي تغامزوا وتضاحكوا

RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r6.claim: To explain the syntax, one may supply ‘that we leave doing what we wish,’ coordinating the phrase with what their fathers worshipped.
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r6.anchor: التقدير : أصلواتك تأمرك أن نترك ما يعبد آباؤنا وأن نترك فعل ما نشاء

RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r7.claim: Alternatively, prayer both commands them to abandon idols and forbids them from doing whatever they wish with their money.
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r7.anchor: أن تجعل الصلاة آمرة وناهية والتقدير : أصلواتك تأمرك بأن نترك عبادة الأوثان وتنهاك أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء

RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r8.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r8.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads both verbs in the second person, ‘or that you do with our wealth what you wish’; this refers to Shuʿayb’s demand to stop short measure and fraud and accept little lawful gain over abundant unlawful gain.
RAZI-FULL:v18p36/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة { أو أن * تفعل * فى أموالنا ما * تشاء } بتاء الخطاب فيهما

RAZI-FULL:v18p36#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p36#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p36#2/r1.claim: One interpretation is sarcastic inversion: they call Shuʿayb foolish and ignorant while using the opposite words.
RAZI-FULL:v18p36#2/r1.anchor: أن يكون المعنى إنك لأنت السفيه الجاهل إلا أنهم عكسوا ذلك على سبيل الاستهزاء والسخرية به

RAZI-FULL:v18p36#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p36#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p36#2/r2.claim: A second reading is that he was considered forbearing and right-guided in his own eyes or by his people.
RAZI-FULL:v18p36#2/r2.anchor: أن يكون المراد إنك موصوف عند نفسك وعند قومك بالحلم والرشد

RAZI-FULL:v18p36#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p36#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p36#2/r3.claim: Al-Razi prefers that they acknowledge Shuʿayb was renowned for sound judgment, then mockingly ask how such a man can forbid their ancestral religion.
